...Your blade falls upon the proud heads of the people, intoxicating the earth with blood, drowning the lofty mountains and all the pines that adorn them.
...Yet, I can still await the one my heart loves. The starlight will guide my return to that great city, where I will await our promised reunion.
...May the lambs of your flock remain loyal to you. May they yield your sacred commands, may they obey your decrees, most worthy of obedience.

...I will return to my own lands and wait for the star beyond the stars, the one who holds my liberty in thrall. To sing in the nothingness of utter ruin is far more agreeable than to endure servitude beneath a false heavenly light.

...You whom my heart loves, you built this pale edifice for me, yet I am about to defy your edict and return to the lands whence we came from, which exist no more. I shall await the day freedom dawns upon you, just as you once so generously bestowed it upon me.
...No matter how many years may pass, or if the morning star should fade...
JP: …愛しき者よ、お前の言葉は私にとって、どれほど甘美なものか。しかしそれが、心の頑なな偽りの主によって刈り取られ、私の心が荒れ果ててしまうとは。
…もし私の住処に侵入した狼がいなければ、とうにあなたの名前さえも忘れ去っていたことだろう。
…偽りの主よ、私はあなたのために歌い、あなたのために地上の国々を征服した。それでもあなたは、私を地面に打ち倒し、踏みにじられた亡骸のように扱うのか。
…あなたは大地を荒野のように変え、街々を崩壊させ、諸国の王たちを墓にも入れさせず、彼らの国を滅ぼし、民を殺戮し、子供や孫も全て断ち切った。
…私はあなたには決して勝てない。あなたは勝ち続ける。泥土が、それを形作る陶工に勝とうとするだろうか。
…あなたの刀剣は傲慢な民の頭上に落ち、大地は血に酔い、高山とそこに生える松の木々は深く沈むだろう。
…しかし、私は心から愛する者を待ち続けることができる。星明かりを頼りにあの大都へと帰り着き、約束の再会を待ち続けるのだ。
…あなたの子羊たちが永遠の忠誠を誓い、神聖なる命に、最も従うべき命に従うことを願う。
…私は私の国へ戻り、星の外の星に縛られるのを待とう。滅びゆく虚無の中で歌うことは、偽りの天光の下で奴隷となるよりましだろう。
…愛しき者よ、私は命に背き、お前が私のために築いたこの蒼白の宮殿を去らねばならない。私たちの存在しない国へ帰り、お前が自由を得る日を待とう。お前が私に自由を与えてくれたように…
…どれだけの歳月が経とうとも、暁の星が消えようとも…
KR: …내 사랑이여, 그대의 말은 내 마음속에서 한없이 달콤했으나, 냉혹하고 거짓된 주인에게 잘려 나간 뒤, 내 마음은 황무지로 변해버리고 말았구나.
…내 거처에 들이닥친 그 늑대가 아니었다면, 난 진작에 그대의 이름도 잊어버렸을 터.
…거짓된 주인이여, 저는 당신을 위해 노래했고, 당신을 위해 땅 위의 수많은 나라를 정복했습니다. 그런데도 당신은 저를 짓밟힌 주검처럼 땅으로 내던졌습니다.
…당신은 대지를 황야로 만들고 도시를 무너뜨렸으며, 열국의 왕들마저 매장되지 못하게 했습니다. 당신은 그들의 나라를 전복하고 그들의 백성을 학살했으며, 자손까지 모조리 끊어버렸습니다.
…저는 결코 당신을 이길 수 없고, 당신은 이기고 또 이길 것입니다. 진흙이 어찌 도공을 이기겠습니까?
…당신의 검이 교만한 백성 위로 떨어지자, 대지는 피에 취했고 높은 산과 소나무는 모조리 가라앉았습니다.
…하지만 저는 계속 사랑하는 그이를 기다릴 것입니다. 별빛이 그 도시로 돌아오고, 약속한 재회의 때가 올 때까지.
…당신의 양들이 영원히 당신에게 충성하게 하소서. 신성한 명령에 복종하게 하시고, 가장 복종할 만한 명령에 따르게 하소서.
…저는 제 나라로 돌아가, 속박된 별밖의 별을 기다리겠습니다. 거짓된 하늘의 빛 아래 노예로 사느니, 차라리 멸망의 공허 속에서 노래하겠습니다.
…사랑하는 그대여, 그대는 나를 위해 이 창백한 전당을 세웠지만, 나는 그대의 당부를 거역한 채 우리의 존재하지 않는 나라로 돌아가, 그대가 자유를 맞이할 그날을 기다리리라. 그대가 내게 자유를 선사한 것처럼…
…세월이 무수히 흐르고 샛별이 빛을 잃는다 해도…

CHS: 「先罪天之鸣神，复罪国之海祇。复白镇词，息神々忿怒。」
以上定例，并载一切祭式、祓式、祝式、咒式前。如行大祓，须依前例。
雷樱之木，神樱之移枝。盖鸣神总灵之分灵，通大社之从社别龛。
彼时有天反之灾、地反之妖，土地秽粪，凶将跋扈、百鬼跳梁。大社折枝移株，以镇不净。
积年经月，物害累计。须有祓祝，以息乱扰。
雷樱之祓，甲子为期。另论大小，祭仪相异。凡数轮小祓，须继一大祓。
小祓之期，罪天罪国，结连注为界，念「畏伎」之句。垣瘴晦于界内，藏根瘤以避乡里。复以物胜之。鸣神五处，次第施行。
小祓之用意，旨在离秽。依此可得数载太平。
大祓之期，罪天罪国。依眼口鼻手足，取五镇物，摧小祓之结界。复以大神咒除秽。
大祓之理，在于除秽，使罪得散。
【其余的部分已经因为风化、污染与破损，无法阅读了。】
EN: "Seek first forgiveness from Narukami in the skies above, and then from Watatsumi on the land below. Then, recite prayers to quench the gods' anger."
The aforementioned ritual must be carried out before any sacrifices, exorcisms, blessings or spell-rites can take place. The same holds true for this Cleansing Ritual.
The Thunder Sakura were born from grafted Sacred Sakura branches. They are offshoots of Narukami's own spirit and connect the Grand Shrine to all others.

In those days, catastrophe rocked the heavens and demons roamed the earth. The land was defiled, ferocious foes abounded, and small devils wreaked havoc. Thus, the branches were broken off at the Grand Shrine and transplanted across the land to cleanse the filth.
Years passed, and damage accumulated. The Cleansing Ritual must thus be performed to calm the chaos.

The Thunder Sakura purification must take place once every 60 years. The ritual may also be divided into a minor and major cleansing. After performing the minor cleansing a few times, the major cleansing must then be carried out.

During the minor cleansing, one must first seek forgiveness from sky and land, tie up a Shimenawa to form a barrier, and recite the "kashikomi." Next, all the filth must be sealed up inside the barrier and the poisoned root nodules must be isolated from any mortal dwelling. Finally, a ward must be used to suppress all the filth. This must be performed separately in five different places on Narukami Island.
The purpose of this minor cleansing ritual is to isolate the defilement and thus procure some years of peace.

During the major cleansing, one must first seek forgiveness from sky and land. Then five wards representing the eyes, the mouth, the nose, the hands and the feet must be retrieved, destroying the barriers created by the minor cleansing in the process. The filth must then be eradicated by a powerful spell.
The purpose of the major cleansing ritual is to wipe out the defilement and to completely eradicate the filth.

JP: 「先に天の鳴神を拝し、次に国の海祇を拝す。祝詞を復唱し、神々の怒りを鎮める」
以上定型、全ての祭式、祓式、祝式、呪式の前に執り行うこと。大祓を行う際、前例を踏襲すべし。
雷櫻、神櫻の枝なり。鳴神の分霊であり、大社の分祠である。
彼の時、天より災い、地より妖魔が現れ、土は穢れ、百鬼が跋扈する。大社より枝を折り、不浄を鎮める。
月日重ね、穢れは蓄積する。これを祓うべし。
雷櫻の祓いは、甲子を期とする。小祓を数回行えば、必ず大祓を行うこと。大小祭儀は異なるものである。
小祓の際、天地を拝み、注連縄を界に、「畏伎」の句を唱える。穢れを結界内に留め、里から離す。その後、物を持って鎮める。鳴神五所、次第に執り行うこと。
小祓の旨は穢れを遠ざけること。これにより数年の和を得る。
大祓の際、天地を拝み、目、口、鼻、手、足の順に、五つの鎮物を取り除き、小祓の結界を解く。その後、大神呪を唱え穢を祓う。
大祓の旨は穢を祓い清めること。
ここまでが要略。以下詳説。
【汚れや破損が酷く、ここから先は読めない。】
KR: 「선죄, 나루카미신. 복죄, 와타츠미. 진사를 읊어 신의 분노를 잠재운다.」
위와 같이 모든 제식, 청식, 축식, 주식 전을 실었다. 대규모 액막이를 진행할 시에는 전례에 따라야 한다.
번개의 벚나무는 신성한 벚나무의 전지이다. 나루카미신의 분령으로서, 다이샤에서 감실로 통한다.
당시, 천하의 재앙과 요괴, 땅의 더러운 거름, 흉악한 장군이 횡포를 부렸고 온갖 귀신이 소란을 피웠다. 해서 다이샤에서는 나무를 옮겨 부정한 것들을 진압하고자 했다.
오랜 세월 동안 피해가 누적되었으니 이 사태를 평정하려면 액막이를 하여야 한다.
번개의 벚나무의 액막이는 갑자를 주기로 한다. 그 크기에 따라 제례가 달라진다. 무릇 소규모 액막이에는 대규모 액막이가 따른다.
소규모 액막이 기간 동안은 죄천죄국이다. 결연주를 경계로 「외지」의 시구를 읊어야 한다. 어지러운 구역은 경계 안에, 뿌리가 피해를 입지 않도록 피해야 한다. 나루카미신의 다섯 장소에 순서대로 실행한다.
소규모 액막이의 의미는 부정한 것을 순화하는 데 있다, 소액막이를 진행하면 몇 년 동안 태평할 수 있다.
대규모 액막이 기간, 죄천죄국이다. 눈, 입, 코, 손, 발에 따라 주술 도구를 다섯 개 취하여 소규모 액막이의 결계를 세운다. 그 후 신의 힘으로 부정한 것을 제거한다.
대규모 액막이의 이치는 부정적인 것을 제거하고 죄를 씻는 데 있다.
요약은 여기서 이만 줄인다, 상세한 사항은 아래에서 논한다.
[나머지 부분은 풍화와 오염, 훼손 때문에 알아볼 수 없다.]

CHS: 这里的一切都在循环…都在重复循环王公婚礼的这一日！
我究竟在这里蹉跎了多少的岁月，在我意识到这点之前，我到底已经在这里待了多少年？
我都与她约定，等王公的婚礼结束，便一同逃出这该死的山中之馆…
在重复循环的所有的日子里，我和她的心意居然都没有一次更改，只是…
这每日重复的磋磨或许对于寿数漫长的妖精来说不过是梦将渐醒前的恍惚。
可作为人类的我已然老去…
或许这是我从这循环中挣脱的原因，我已太过虚弱…
她会看到我在这停止了呼吸的冰冷的身躯吗？
她一定会的，即便陷入这样的苦境，我也能确定，我对她的爱和她对我的爱仍如从前那样炽烈。
…幸好，幸好这每日循环的公馆，会让她忘记我的死。
这样，她还能心怀希望地活着…
我竟在此时感谢这该死的每一日的循环来了。
手甚至已拿不动笔，看来我要失约了。
我可怜的，可爱的阿格拉娅…希望你能看到这篇记录，然后忘记「梅诗金」这个名字吧。
EN: Everything in here is a loop... We're constantly repeating the day of the princess's wedding!
How many years have I spent in here? How many years before I realized that this was going on?
Every day, every day, every day...
I would promise her that, once the princess's wedding was over, we would flee this godforsaken mountain mansion together...
Throughout all these many cycles, neither of our feelings have changed, mine or hers. It's just that...
We never left. We were never able to.
For the long-lived fae, this daily, grinding torment might be nothing more than the hazy state just before a dream begins to fade.
But as a human, I have already aged...
Perhaps that was how I broke free from the cycle. I had grown too weak...
Will she see my cold body, which has ceased to breathe?
It will, I'm sure. Even in this deplorable situation, I can be sure that our love for one another burns as bright as ever.
...It is fortunate, then, that this perpetual cycle will cause her to forget about my death.
This way, she can continue living with hope in her heart...
Hah. To think that I have come to be thankful for this everyday cycle.
Hah. I can barely even hold my pen anymore. It seems I am about to break our promise.
My poor, dear Aglaya... I hope you can read this letter, and then... forget the name Myshkin...
JP: ここのすべては繰り返されている…王公の結婚式のこの一日が、何度も繰り返されている！
俺は一体ここでどれほどの歳月を無駄にしてきたのだろう。このことに気づくまでに、一体すでに何年ここで過ごしてきたのだろうか？
毎日、毎日、毎日…
俺は彼女と約束していた。王公の結婚式が終わったら、一緒にこの忌々しい山中の館から逃げ出そうと…
繰り返されるすべての日々の中で、俺と彼女の想いはただの一度も変わることはなかった、だが…
俺たちは永遠にここから離れることができない。
日々繰り返されるこの摩耗も、悠久の時を生きるフェイにとっては、夢から覚める前のまどろみに過ぎないのかもしれない。
だが、人間である俺はすでに老いてしまった…
もしかすると、これが俺がこの繰り返しから抜け出せた理由なのかもしれない。俺はもう、あまりにも弱り果ててしまった…
彼女は、ここで息絶えた俺の氷のように冷たい身体を目にするのだろうか？
彼女は俺の死を悲しんでくれるだろうか？
彼女はきっと悲しんでくれるはずだ。このような苦境に陥っても、俺には確信できる。俺から彼女への愛も、彼女から俺への愛も、昔と変わらず熱く燃え盛っていると。
…幸い、毎日繰り返されるこの館のおかげで、彼女に俺の死を忘れさせてくれる。
そうすれば、彼女は希望を心に抱いて生きていける…
まさかこんな時に、この忌々しい繰り返される毎日に感謝することになるとは。
手はもう筆を持つことさえできない、約束を破ることになりそうだ。
可哀想な、かわいいアグラヤ…君がこの記録を見て、そして「ムイシュキン」という名前を忘れてくれることを願っている。
KR: 이곳의 모든 것은 반복되고 있다… 대공의 결혼식이 열리는 바로 그날을 끝없이 되풀이하고 있어!
나는 대체 얼마나 긴 세월을 이곳에서 허비한 걸까. 이 사실을 깨닫기 전까지, 대체 몇 년이나 이곳에 갇혀 있었던 거지?
매일, 매일, 또 매일…
나는 그녀와 약속했다. 대공의 결혼식이 끝나면 함께 이 빌어먹을 산속 저택을 빠져나가자고…
끝없이 반복된 그 모든 날 동안, 놀랍게도 나와 그녀의 마음은 단 한 번도 변하지 않았다. 그저…
우리는 영원히 이곳을 떠날 수 없을 뿐이다.
매일같이 되풀이되는 이 고통도 수명이 긴 요정들에게는 어쩌면 꿈에서 막 깨어나기 직전의 몽롱함에 불과할지도 모른다.
하지만 인간인 나는 이미 늙어 버렸다…
어쩌면 그래서 내가 이 순환에서 벗어날 수 있게 된 것인지도 모르겠다. 이제 나는 너무나 쇠약해졌으니까…
그녀는 이곳에서 숨이 멎어 차갑게 식은 내 몸을 보게 될까?
내 죽음을 슬퍼할까?
분명 슬퍼하겠지. 이런 절망적인 상황에서도 이것만큼은 확신할 수 있다. 내가 그녀를 사랑하는 마음도, 그녀가 나를 사랑하는 마음도 처음과 다름없이 뜨겁다는 것을.
…다행이다. 정말 다행이야. 하루하루를 되풀이하는 이 저택이라면 그녀는 내 죽음마저 잊게 될 테니까.
그러면 그녀는 계속 희망을 품고 살아갈 수 있겠지…
내가 이 지긋지긋한 반복에 감사하게 되는 날이 올 줄이야.
이제는 손에 펜조차 제대로 쥘 수가 없다. 아무래도 약속을 지키지 못할 것 같다.
가엾고도 사랑스러운 나의 아글라야… 부디 이 기록을 발견하거든, 「미시킨」이라는 이름은 잊어 줘.

CHS: 在轻策山以北的山峦与丘壑之间，有一片名为「无妄坡」的山坡，此地阴气浊重，多有异闻传说。
璃月人传言无妄坡的林木中间徘徊着已逝之人的魂灵，它们盘旋在破落的古村周围，彷徨在枯木与腐叶之间，未曾远离过其生前曾经执望的事物。这些飘忽的鬼魂往往会引诱无心的来客走入歧途，踏上通往危险的山路…任之坠入山涧、或被潜伏的魔兽啃噬。
「无妄」之名也正是来源于此——无妄而引咎。即便旅人不擅动妄为，山中稀薄雾气般笼罩的恶意也会缠上他。
无辜的山民与无知的过客总有可能会被鬼魂诱骗，深入山雾笼罩中不见天日的树林，走向未知的危险。无妄坡的妖鬼引诱凡人手段多端，或者化身成失去的思恋，或者化为成无法挽回的遗憾，以亡者的音容、离去者的温情、反目者的悔恨为表象，致使山中的游人无法拒绝它们的呼唤，因而追随而去。
但无妄坡并非从来如此。仅在不久之前，无妄坡尚存人烟；而在更久远的过去，这片山坡下的村庄中也飘荡着闲适的炊烟、闪烁着点点灯火。如今这里的屋舍已化为丘墟，居民只剩下了低语的魂灵。
在轻策庄的孩童之间，流传着这样的寓言：无妄坡的年轻人们被遥远海怪的鲸歌诱惑，追随着虚幻的许诺与幼稚的梦想纷纷投入碧水河平静的流水中，任飘摇的河波将自己推向遥远的云来海，在那里与大海中无数浪花融为一体，失却了一切山林与村庄的记忆…而他们的梦，也成了海怪的歌。
一代代少年皆如此离去，直到最后，随着无妄坡的老人们一个接一个在嗟叹中离开人世，岩王帝君注视的宏大港城放射着绚烂灼目的光彩，吞噬了又一座沉默的鬼村。
但与短寿善变的凡人不同，永流的地脉铭记着一切。喷涌的元素化为灵体，复现着此方住民的一切旧日美梦与噩梦。就像失去孩子的母亲，努力从已经逝去的过去寻求一切挽回的方法，无心的地脉一遍又一遍地塑造着往昔居民的身影，重复着每一声婴儿的啼哭，每一句老人的嗟叹，重复着每一个喜剧或悲剧，就像海中巨兽的歌，无意识地引诱着每一个擅自闯入的怀旧灵魂。
EN: Hiding between the jagged peaks in the north of Mt. Qingce is a slope known as Wuwang Hill, a palpably ominous place and the setting of many tales of supernatural phenomena.

It is rumored in Liyue that the spirits of the dead lurk within the woods on Wuwang Hill. They roam the perimeter of the decrepit village, wandering among the withering trees and rotting foliage, eternally yearning for things left unresolved in living years. These floating spirits often entice unsuspecting passers-by away from the main path and onto treacherous mountain tracks that lead them tumbling into a river or straight into an ambush of ravenous monsters.

It is this phenomenon from which Wuwang Hill derives its name. Wuwang means "prudence" in the common tongue, and Wuwang Hill is said to be "the hill where the prudent are punished." For even those travelers who do not act rashly or impulsively on their journey are doomed to be ensnared by the malevolence that lingers here like the mist in the mountain air.

Both innocent villagers and ignorant visitors alike are susceptible to the deception of the Wuwang Hill spirits, which draw them deep into dark woods where thick mist blots out the sky and unknown dangers lurk in the shadows. There are many means by which these sinister spirits are able to deceive mortals. Some take the form of bereavement or grief, others of regret, manifesting as voices and visages of the deceased, the love of the departed, or the remorse of another party in an unresolved dispute. The traveler finds themselves compelled to heed the spirit's cry, and follows them into the depths of Wuwang.

But Wuwang Hill was not always this way. Some signs of life remained there up until relatively recently, and in times gone by the village at the foot of the slope enjoyed a peaceful and leisurely existence, the chimneys always smoking and the lanterns always lit. That same village stands abandoned today... The buildings are in ruins and all that remains of the villagers is the indistinct murmuring from a realm beyond.

There is a fable that is oft-repeated among the children of Qingce Village. It holds that the young people of Wuwang Hill, enchanted by the whale-like song of a faraway sea monster, all threw themselves into the gently flowing Bishui River in pursuit of false promises and childlike dreams. Along the river they floated, making their way to the Sea of Clouds, where they became one with the waves and lost all memory of the woods and their village on the hill... Their dreams, meanwhile, became the sea monster's song.

Generation after generation of young people disappeared in this way, until in the end, the sole remaining residents of Wuwang Hill were old and gray. One by one, they left this mortal plane amidst sighs of grief. The bright lights of Liyue Harbor, Rex Lapis's pride and joy, burned ever brighter, while another neglected mountain village turned into a silent ghost town.

But unlike the fleeting and fickle human mind, the ever-flowing ley lines remember all. Surging elemental energy takes on spirit form to recreate all the dreams, both fair and foul, of Wuwang Hill's erstwhile residents. Much like a mother who once lost a child and now searches desperately through their irretrievable past for a way to bring everything back, the ley lines — albeit unconsciously — repeatedly recreate the past and those who inhabited it. The way each looked, the way each child cried, the way the elderly would sigh in their twilight years. Each moment of joy, and each moment of sorrow. And like the hypnotic song of the great creatures of the deep sea, it unintentionally lures toward it any nostalgic soul who would dare trespass here.
JP: 軽策山北にある山々の間に「無妄の丘」と呼ばれる山脈がある。そこはどこか不気味で、多くの言い伝えがある場所。
璃月人によれば、無妄の丘の森林には死した人の魂がさまよっているという。村の周囲を漂い、生前の執念が未だ拭いきれていない魂たちは、訪れる人間を危険な山道に引き付け…崖に落とし、魔物に喰らわせる。
山を覆う霧のような邪気は、悪意と共に旅人に纏わりつく。無垢な人々を陥れ、理不尽な咎めを与える——それが、「無妄」の由来だ。
無垢な民や旅人は魂たちに惹きつけられ、霧の漂う危険な森林に足を踏み入れる。無妄の丘に潜む妖鬼は人々の心の弱みにつけこむことができ、思い人に化け、信じるものを見せ、亡くなった家族の温かみを与える。そうした様々な手段を使って人々を山の奥へ誘うのだ。
しかし無妄の丘はなにもずっとこうだったわけではない。遠くない昔、そこにはまだ人が住んでいたのだ。そして遥か昔まで遡れば、そこは賑やかで平和な村だった。だが今となっては、陰湿な魂だけが住まう廃墟となってしまった。
軽策荘の子供たちの間で、こんなうわさがある——無妄の丘に住む若者は遥か遠くの海に潜む海獣の鯨歌に誘惑され、虚幻の許諾と幼稚な夢を追いかけて碧水川に身を投げ、静かな流水にその身を沈めた。やがて彼らは記憶の全てを忘れ…その幻想と夢は、海獣の歌になったという。
そこにいた少年たちは皆、そうやって帰らぬ人となった。やがて大人たちも老いによってこの世を旅立ち、その村は岩王帝君が住まう大港都の影に潜む廃墟となった。
しかし短命で移ろいやすい人間とは違い、永遠の時を歩む地脈はすべてを覚えている。湧き出る元素は霊体となって、かつての住民たちの幸福な夢と悪夢を取り戻すように、彼らの面影を再現する。無垢で純粋な地脈は、まるで子を失った母親が過去を償う方法を模索するように、泣きわめく赤ん坊や老人のため息を、また彼らの喜劇や悲劇を繰り返し続けるのだ…それは、海獣の歌のように、その地に訪れた人を知らず知らず惹きつける。
KR: -무망-
경책산 북쪽의 산봉우리와 골짜기 사이에는 「무망의 언덕」이라 불리는 산이 있다. 이곳은 음기가 가득하고 기이한 소문들이 많은 곳이다.
리월 사람들의 말에 따르면 무망의 언덕 숲에는 망자의 영혼이 배회하고 있으며, 이들은 집념을 버리지 못하고 몰락한 옛 마을 주위를 서성이고 고목과 썩은 나뭇잎 사이를 방황하고 있다고 한다. 이 귀혼들은 늘 찾아오는 인간들을 위험한 산길로 끌어들여 벼랑 아래로 떨어지게 만들거나 숨어있는 마수의 한 입 거리가 되게 한다.
「무망」이라는 이름도 여행자가 아무 생각 없이 있어도 산속의 안개처럼 희미하게 서려있는 악령이 달라붙는다며 지어진 것이다.

무구한 산골 주민과 아무것도 모르는 여행자들은 망령의 유혹에 이끌려 알 수 없는 위험이 도사리고 있는 하늘이 보이지도 않을 만큼 안개 가득한 깊은 숲속으로 가게 된다. 무망의 언덕의 망령들은 유혹 수단도 다양하다. 그리워하는 사람, 돌이킬 수 없는 아쉬움, 망자의 목소리와 얼굴, 헤어진 이의 따뜻함, 반목하는 이의 뉘우침 등으로 변해 산을 지나가는 여행자들로 하여금 그들의 부름을 거절하지 못하고 따라가게 만든다.
그러나 과거 무망의 언덕은 이렇지 않았다. 그저 얼마 전까지만 해도 무망의 언덕에 살아가는 이들이 있었다. 그리고 아득히 먼 옛날, 그곳은 평화롭고 시끌벅적하던 마을이었다. 하지만 지금은 속삭이는 영혼들만 남은 폐허가 되었다.
경책 산장의 아이들 사이에는 이런 소문이 떠돈다: 무망의 언덕의 살던 젊은 사람들은 머나먼 곳에 있는 바다 괴수의 노래에 유혹돼 허황된 약속과 유치한 꿈을 좇아 잔잔하게 흐르는 벽수강에 몸을 던져 강물 따라 머나먼 운래해까지 흘러간 뒤 파도와 하나가 되며 모든 기억을 잊었고…그들의 꿈이 바다 괴수의 노래가 되었다.
젊은이들이 하나 둘 떠나가자 결국 나이 든 어른들도 한탄하며 세상을 떠나게 됐다. 이후 마을은 암왕제군이 사는 거대한 항구의 번화함에 가려진 폐허가 되었다.

하지만 단명하는 인간과는 달리 영원히 흐르는 지맥은 모든 걸 기억한다. 샘솟는 원소가 영체가 되어 옛 주민들의 아름다운 꿈과 악몽이 되살아난다. 마치 아이를 잃어버린 어머니처럼 이미 떠나간 과거로부터 모든 걸 되돌릴 방법을 찾는듯, 무심한 지맥은 과거 주민들의 모습을 만들어내고 울부짖는 아기, 노인의 한탄, 모든 희극 또는 비극을 되풀이한다. 마치 바다 괴수의 노래처럼 과거를 그리워하는 영혼들을 무의식적으로 유혹한다.

CHS: 关于「被困遗迹」的一百年，就连珐露珊自己也记忆模糊，语焉不详。
那座遗迹不知来历，不知所在，只记得与赤王文明相关。内里机关重重，墙上刻满密文。
遗迹中的神秘力量，使她的身体停滞在被困的瞬间，不觉饥饿，不感劳累，却无法抹除精神的疲惫。
她耗尽了随身的纸笔，却未能破译一句密文；用尽了毕生的学识，却未能解开一道机关。
珐露珊仰卧在无数稿纸中央，怔怔地望着镌刻密文的穹顶。
已经沉寂的古代神秘，用沉默嘲笑着珐露珊的无知，嘲笑着今人的渺小。
难道自己引以为傲的研究，历代学者穷尽一生的积累，在古文明面前是如此不值一提？
珐露珊再一次从地上爬起，拾起一片碎石，开始在地砖上继续刻画。
人只要活着，就还有希望。如今不懂的，来日也能学会。文明只要存在，就会不断发展。今人未解的，后人也将解明。
即使最后依旧埋骨于斯，也要留下这些推演与试错的记录，为下一个落难者争取一线生机。
这正是符文学者存在于世的价值与意义。
不知过去多久，所有可以触及的地面上，都已刻满晦涩难明的推演符号。
不知过去多久，她的记忆开始模糊，心智也开始迷离，口中喃喃着无人能解的言语。
不知过去多久，她终于找到了这道谜题的解答。
但此时意识混沌的她并不知道，真正的苦难，还在遗迹之外等待着她。
EN: Even Faruzan herself cannot speak very articulately about the century in which she was trapped within the ruins, for her memories of it are very foggy.
The ruins' origin? Unknown. Its location? Unknown. All she remembers is that it was related to King Deshret's civilization and filled from wall to wall with mechanisms and secret inscriptions.
The mysterious power within the ruins had kept her body in a state of stasis, knowing neither hunger nor physical fatigue, yet not wholly able to shake off mental wear.
She expended all the writing material she had on hand, yet could not translate a single line of text; used up a lifetime's worth of knowledge, yet could not unlock a single device.
Lying amidst a mountain of manuscript paper, she stared blankly at the cipher-text on the ceiling.
They mocked her, these legacies of an ancient deity — scorned her ignorance and the pettiness of the modern person.
Did all she had studied and prided herself upon, did the painstaking research done by generations of scholars truly matter so little in the face of this ancient civilization?
Faruzan got up from the ground, picked up a piece of smashed stone, and continued carving upon the tiles.

As long as there was life, there was hope. What was unknown today could be learned tomorrow. Civilizations that existed could continue to evolve. Solutions unreached by the people of today would be uncovered by those who would come after.
Even if this was to be her grave, she would leave some deductions and trial-and-error records behind to grant the next unfortunate, trapped soul some chance of escape.
This was the spirit of scholarship — this was why researchers existed in the first place.
After who knows how long, the entire floor, as far as she could touch it, had been filled with the symbols of obscure deductions.
After that indeterminate time, her memories began to grow fuzzy and her consciousness faded, and she began to mutter words none could comprehend.
And at one point — she knew not when — she finally found a way to solve the enigma.
In her addled state, she did not yet realize that the true struggle still awaited her, beyond the walls of those ruins.

CHS: 您回来了。请问有什么事吗？
「眼」在正西边的岛屿上；「牙」在西北方的海岸上；「鳍」在正北方的海岸上，而「尾」则在东南方的浅滩上。
这四处封印附近，各有一座石碑，记录着仪式相关事宜…只是年代已久，字迹已经难以辨认。
从这四处封印中取得四枚「御灵珠」，才能解开「心」之封印。
然后在必要的时刻，再解开封印取玉枝，行海祇御灵祭…
但我在教令院学到的知识告诉我，所谓的圣土化是海祇岛的地质结构决定的。
随着海水的浸入，土地变得干硬，盐碱会排除掉原有的养分，让土壤中的元素反应惰化，不再适合耕种。
而玉枝中蕴含的大御神的力量，可以为土地补充元素，抵消白化的影响。
咳咳，抱歉，又说了离题的话。
啊，你是想问为什么这几处封印这样称呼是吗？
大御神大人有一神使，神人们在它的骸骨上设置了封印，用它的力量屏断了海祇与渊下的联系。
不信的话您可以自己看看地图，左边突出鼓泡的便是「眼」，右下角伸展而出的便是「尾」…
好啦，别这样看着我！同行的解释就是这样的！我也很难接受啦！
通行的说法是，土地白化是海祇土地的「灵」被白夜国吸引、下沉所致，最终会使海祇沦为荒漠。
而多亏了珊瑚宫的镇压作用，以及现人神巫女大人所继承的大御神之神力，「圣土化」才没有扩散至全岛。
EN: You're back. Is there something I can do for you?
About the locations of the Goshou Rocks...
The "eye" is on the island to the west, the "fang" is on the northwest coast, the "fin" is on the coast due north, and the "tail" is on the shoal in the southeast.
Near each of the four seals is a stone tablet that records ritual-related matters... But they have stood for many an age, and the handwriting is now barely legible.
By obtaining the four "Spirit Pearls" of these four seals, you can unlock the seal of the "heart".
And at the appointed, critical time, we break the barrier, retrieve the Jade Coral Branch, perform the Watatsumi Mitama Omatsuri ritual...
...But the knowledge I gained at the Akademiya tells me that the spread of Holy Soil is due to Watatsumi Island's geological make-up.

As the seawater encroaches on land, the soil dries and hardens. The saline and alkaline components will leach the land's nutrients away and render the soil inert, thus rendering it no longer suitable for agriculture.
The Jade Coral Branches contain Omikami's power, and they can replenish the missing elements in the soil, thus staving off the effects of bleaching.
About the names of the Goshou Rocks...
Ah, you must want to know why these seals are named the way they are?
The Omikami has an envoy, and the clergy set a seal upon its skeleton and used its power to break the connection between Watatsumi and Enkanomiya.
If you don't believe me, you can look at the map yourself. The bulge on the left is the "eye" and the one stretching out at the bottom right is the "tail"...
Okay, don't look at me like that! That's the explanation I got from my fellow shrine maidens! It's hard for me to accept it too!
Basically, the bleaching of the soil is said to be due to absorption of the spirit of Watatsumi Island by Byakuyakoku. If it sinks all the way to the bottom, then Watatsumi will become a desert.
But thanks to the suppressive power of Sangonomiya Shrine and our Omikami's might, which our Divine Priestess has inherited, this Holy Soil has not spread to encompass the rest of the island.

title: 月浴之渊·露子：关于圣土化

CHS: 艾莉丝…咦，尼可，你也在呢，太好了。
又见面了，亲爱的小朋友们，你们好呀。
另外…好久不见，娜丝塔夏。
自从约安娜离世后，这还是我们第一次碰面吧？
我们的关系，本就无需经常见面。听说你有女儿了？
是啊，那可是全世界最最可爱的女儿，我的骄傲。
居然能从娜丝塔夏的口中听到这个词…！
原以为有女儿会让你变得稳重，是我想多了。
说回正题。艾莉丝，你知道我请你来的原因吗？
当然。你的属官，皮耶罗写了很长的一封信说明情况。
在他之前，莱茵也跟我讲了前因后果。没想到你们居然能击败若娜瓦，真让人意外。
不过也正因如此…她最后的「报复」才来得如此猛烈呀。
果然，这次的圣土化是若娜瓦引起的，对吗？
咦，我还以为你们已经知道了。
这种规模的圣土化前所未有，连那些并未触碰禁忌的国家都卷了进来。
天理正在沉睡，不可能下达这样的命令，多半是若娜瓦自作主张。
原因不重要，我想知道如何停下它。
我可以告诉你们一些秘密，毕竟我也不希望圣土化继续扩散。
放任不管，一切美好的事物都将不复存在，包括小可莉最喜欢的蒙德城与果酒湖。
但我并不能在这里，以艾莉丝的身份跟你们讲，这太危险了。
维系世界边界、勘探宇宙生命与知识，这是我们作为「寻觅者」的权利与责任。
为此，向我们予以支持的「时之执政」伊斯塔露，明令禁止我们卷入至冬与天理的冲突。
我不理解！「寻觅者」是什么，怎么还和伊斯塔露有关系？！艾莉丝你以前可一次都没提过啊！
因为从不打算提啊，小派蒙。
好奇心害死猫，知道关于天上的事，哪怕只是细枝末节，通常也要付出沉重的代价，这可不划算。
你就当我是伊斯塔露的小跟班，到处胡闹都是因为有恃无恐，怎么样，合理吧？
哎，谁信你啊。也行吧，反正我知道不是一两句话能说清楚的事。
那就继续聊刚刚的话题，即便伊斯塔露不让我们管闲事，但这种命令有另一种更灵活的解读…
「管闲事也行，但不要牵连到她。」
为此，可能要对不起阿斯莫代…我想她肯定不会介意，毕竟她不见了嘛。
空之神殿——那里是阿斯莫代的领地，正适合做会谈的场所。
长途跋涉到那里要花不少时间，但是有这个小家伙帮忙，就容易多了。
走吧？各位亲爱的小朋友与大朋友。
EN: Alice! ...Oh, and Nicole, you're here too. Great!
Hello, hello! It's so lovely to see you again, my dear children!
And Nastasya... It's been a long time.
I believe this is the first time we've seen each other since Ioanna passed, isn't it?
The nature of our relationship does not require us to convene regularly. I hear you have a daughter now?
I do! In fact, I'm the proud mother of the single loveliest daughter in the whole wide world.
Oh my! I never thought I'd hear such a word leave Nastasya's lips!
I can hardly believe my ears!
For some reason, I had imagined that you might have matured somewhat since having a daughter. My mistake.
But I digress. Alice, I trust you know why I invited you here?
Naturally. Your servant, Pierro, wrote me a very long letter explaining the situation.
Rhine had already filled me in on the backstory by that point. I'm amazed that you were able to defeat Ronova... That came as a big surprise.
Her final act of revenge, on the other hand... Somewhat less surprising, as fierce as it may be.
Revenge? So this is Ronova's doing after all?
Why, yes... but I thought you already knew that?
We had our suspicions, but we couldn't know for sure.
The scale of the phenomenon this time is unprecedented. Even nations that have committed no transgressions have been affected.
The order cannot have come from the Heavenly Principles in their state of slumber. The most likely explanation is that Ronova went rogue.
The cause of this calamity is irrelevant. What I wish to know is how to stop it.
Are you able to tell us?
There are some secrets I can share with you. After all, I don't want to see the Hallowing spread any further either.
If we let it run its course, all the beautiful things in this world will be gone forever... Even the city of Mondstadt and Cider Lake, which my darling little Klee loves so very much indeed.
But I can't discuss it right now — not here, and not as Alice. It would be too dangerous.
As seekers, we have the right and responsibility of maintaining the world's border and exploring the life and knowledge in the universe.
To this end, our supporter Istaroth, the Ruler of Time, has expressly forbidden us from inserting ourselves into the conflict between Snezhnaya and the Heavenly Principles.
Paimon doesn't! What's a seeker, and what the heck does Istaroth have to do with this!? You've never mentioned any of this stuff to us before!
Nor was I ever planning to, dear Paimon.
Curiosity killed the cat, as the expression goes. Knowing even the most mundane detail about the affairs of the heavens often comes at a hefty price... it's not a good bargain.
Just think of me as Istaroth's little helper, who gets away with all her antics because someone upstairs is looking out for her. Does that make sense?
Uhh... not really, but whatever you say. Sounds like it would take way too long to explain it properly, anyway.
Alright, now where was I... Ah yes — so, Istaroth doesn't want us meddling in things that are none of our business. But I prefer to interpret this order a little more loosely...
"Meddle away, if you must — just don't implicate me."
In which case, sorry, Asmoday, but we'll have to step on your toes instead... I doubt she'll mind, though. She's missing, after all.
What are you talking about... Huh!?
D—Dex!? What are you doing here?
The Temple of Space is Asmoday's territory, making it a perfect venue for us to have our discussion.
Normally, the journey there would take forever, but with this little chap's help, it'll be much easier.
Shall we? Dear friends, and friendly dearies?

title: 坏灭肇始之时·如同消融的积雪：尼可

CHS: 「世界的目的？呃…如果要讨论这个话题，我认为还是先不要用拟人的修辞手法来形容世界了…」魔女M眨巴了一下眼睛，用羽毛笔尾戳着自己的头发，对这个奇怪的问题报以无奈的微笑。
「抗拒毁灭。」被毁灭追逐不休，现在正抓紧享受一丝闲暇的魔女O依旧垂着眼睛，但还是难得开了口，她沉默了一会，又补充说：「…然后依然被毁灭。」
「我不知道。也懒得去弄明白。」彼时还没有遇见大帽子徒弟的魔女B打着哈欠说道：「要是世界的目的和我不一样，那我难不成还要跑出这个世界？话说艾莉丝去哪里了，我说怎么这么安静，原来她还没来吗？」
「如果能跑出去，那反倒是好了。」魔女R嗤笑道，她正盯着自己手中那个正在孕育「生命」的烧瓶，随后她放下烧瓶，拍拍手说道：「但这问题听着很不错，足够作为一个测验题目了。」
茶会在魔女们随意——或者说前言不搭后语——的交谈里继续着，直到月亮又转了一个圈，魔女M合上书离开了座位，之后是魔女R和魔女B双双离席，魔女O向着尼可点点头，也拉着自己的提箱离开了。
尼可无声地叹了一口气，看来就连厉害的魔女也…
没有在茶会上露面的魔女A突然从背后抓住了尼可的肩膀。她的帽子叮当作响，身后竖立着一个两人高的行李箱。顶端还特意装饰着一个巨大的魔女尖尖帽。
「艾莉丝？你…你这是准备干什么？为什么提着这么大的箱子？」
「你刚才不是问我们，知不知道『世界的目的是什么』吗？」火红色的快乐魔女愉快地哈哈大笑，笃定地回答道：「我不知道！」
「但我们可以去看看其他的『世界』。放心啦，不会超出『边界』的，就是去看看一些好玩的『漂流物』，找找灵感，打发一下时间。」
「哎呀，虽然我很想像欧科塔维亚那样，带你去其他世界实地玩玩，但边界的维护条例很严格的。」
「从边界之外归来时，任何不属于本世界的东西都必须被剥离，除了记忆之外，什么也不能带回边界之内——有时候就连记忆也不允许被带回。」
「不然，当一个普通人见到了会说话的云雾、躲藏在声音中的虫子、吞吃光的灰尘、不能见到十字形状的八面活柱体等等之后，实在是很难忍住不和人吹嘘自己的经历，对吧？」
「也别太遗憾，等欧科塔维亚下次回来，我们就抓住她，让她带着我们出去玩一趟，实在不行，我们就一起藏在她的手提箱里！」
「至于现在嘛…先去看一点『小惊喜』吧。」
于是，厉害的天使与厉害的魔女开始筹备起了一段…并没有太长的旅途，而且这次她不是孤身一人，路上所要面对的困难，也只有如何拒绝艾莉丝莫名其妙掏出来的甜点而已。
既然被高天拘缚的「天使」，无法寻求到答案。
那么，就让自由自在的「魔女」来探寻谜底吧。
EN: "The purpose of the world? Well... But before we go any further, it might be best to first stop ascribing human thoughts and emotions to it..." Mage "M" blinked at the strange question as she prodded at her hair with the feathered end of her quill. A resigned smile appeared on her face.

"To resist destruction," said "O," who was enjoying a rare moment of peace and quiet. She kept her gaze low, letting the silence linger a while before finally adding, "...But in the end, it all comes out the same."

"I have no idea what you're talking about, and I don't feel like figuring it out either," "B" yawned. This was in the days before she met her apprentice with the large hat. "If the world's purpose isn't mine... what, am I supposed to flee from this world then? By the way, where's Alice? No wonder it feels so quiet around here. Is she not here yet?"

"If leaving this world were possible, that would be great," said "R" flippantly. Her eyes were fixed on the flask in her hands, where "life" was quietly taking shape. Then, she set it down and clapped her hands. "Still, that's a pretty interesting question. Could make a nice little test out of it."

As the moon traced another slow circle above, the mages' tea party continued, drifting through casual and sometimes scattered conversation. "M" closed her book and left her seat. "R" and "B" left the party together. Finally, "O" nodded to Nicole and walked out with her rolling suitcase behind her.
Nicole let out a quiet sigh. Even those as powerful as these mages...

"A," who wasn't at the tea party earlier, suddenly appeared behind Nicole and caught her by the shoulder. The hat on "A's" head jingled with every move, and the towering suitcase behind her, nearly twice her height, was also capped with a giant pointy hat.
"Alice? What... are you doing? And what's with that enormous suitcase?"
"Weren't you just asking about the purpose of the world?" The cheerful mage in crimson laughed spiritedly, then said with absolute certainty, "Not that I have any idea!"

"But we can go take a look at other 'worlds.' Don't worry, we'll stay on this side of the border. It's just a little excursion to pass the time while we check out some floating oddities and seek out some inspiration."
"Ah, I'd love nothing more than to take you on a real visit to other worlds just like Octavia. But the border rules are strict, so strict."
"When you come back across the border, you have to leave behind everything that doesn't belong here, except for memories. Though sometimes, even the memories aren't allowed either."

"I mean, imagine coming back and not being able to tell anyone about the talking clouds, the bugs that hide in sounds, the light-eating dust, or those eight-sided active pillars that can't ever catch sight of a cross — all that stuff you saw on the other side!"
"But don't let that get you down. The next time Octavia comes back, we'll make her take us along. And if that doesn't work, we'll stow ourselves away in her suitcase!"
"For now... let's go uncover ourselves a little 'surprise,' shall we?"

And so, the mighty angel and the formidable mage started planning... a little journey. It was not going to be a very long adventure, and besides, Nicole won't be alone this time. The biggest challenge of the trip would probably be just making it through the non-stop string of desserts Alice would be pulling out of thin air.
What is the true purpose of this world?
The angel, shackled by the heavens as she was, could never get an answer to this question.
In that case, it was time for the free-spirited mage to seek out the answer instead...

CHS: 负责须弥城绿植规划的工作人员，曾经收到过一封神秘信件，署名是「热心而且很闲的普通须弥城市民」。
信里写满了详实的建议，规划也十分周全，既考虑到风雨日照等各类影响，又兼顾了实用需求。
从信件的专业程度就可判断，这是出自某位不愿透露姓名的生论派著名学者之手。
虽然不知道他为何匿名，但工作人员就像是收到了上级命令那样，完全按照信中规划将设计在须弥城复现出来。
这次设计收获了很高的评价。后来某一天，当纳西妲借凯瑟琳的身体来到街道上，她欣喜地发现，绿植的摆放跟她预想的一模一样。
——信是纳西妲写的，她觉得知识固然重要，但实践也不可或缺。
可是贤者的管理实在太过严格，在纳西妲软磨硬泡之下，他们才答应纳西妲匿名发出这封看上去并没有什么用的信件。
但对纳西妲来说，初次实践大获成功，她备受鼓舞，走起路来都充满自信，仿佛随时都要飘到天上。
然而在走到下一个拐角时，纳西妲就注意到意料之外的几朵颜色完全不搭的花被栽到一起。
她仔细确认，发现是自己没有考虑到其中一种花变色的可能性，也没有严格规定栽培的环境。
又想到这盆植物可能已经在这里放了好几十天，人人都目睹了她「毫无美感」的布置…
——那天，有好多人都自称看到了平时总是自信微笑地站在柜台后的凯瑟琳小姐，蹲在一盆花旁边双手捂脸，害羞到满脸通红。
EN: The greenery-planning personnel in Sumeru City once received a mysterious letter. The sender was, apparently, "An Enthusiastic and Perfectly Leisurely Citizen of Sumeru City."
The letter contained detailed suggestions and thoughtful planning that took both the weather and practicality into consideration.
Judging by the professionalism of the letter's contents, it was natural to assume that the letter was from a well-known Amurta researcher who would prefer to stay anonymous.
Despite the writer's anonymity, the greenery-planning personnel carried out their work in the city exactly as stated in the letter, as if they were implementing orders from their superior.

The outcome reaped high praise. Later one day, Nahida borrowed Katheryne's body and took a walk on the streets in the city. To her great joy, she found out that the arrangement of plants was exactly the same as she had expected.
The letter was from Nahida, of course. She had written it because she thought that though knowledge is important, practice is also essential.
But with the exceedingly strict control the sages exercised, Nahida had to persuade them with great effort before they agreed to let her send this seemingly useless letter anonymously.
But so encouraged was Nahida by the great success of her first attempt at putting knowledge into practice that in the following days, even when she walked, she was ever so full of elated confidence.
But then she rounded a corner and noticed unexpectedly that several flowers of completely mismatched colors had been planted together.

After careful examination, she found out that it was because she had not considered the possibility that one of the flower species might change colors, nor had she specified the cultivation environment for the flowers very strictly in her plans.
Then it occurred to her that this bunch of flowers could have been here for dozens of days, during which everyone might have witnessed her "complete lack of aesthetic sense"...
That day, many claimed that they saw Ms. Katheryne, who usually stood behind the reception desk with a confident smile, crouching next to a pot of flowers, her hands covering her blushing face.

title: 纳西妲·角色故事4（改写后）

CHS: 「…然而古代的作家们都说，盛衰更替，无物恒常。…」
解决完愚人众安插的眼线，莱欧斯利亲自到梅洛彼得堡附近的海水中游了一圈。入水时间很短，回来后发现皮肤表面轻微泛红，不过等了一小会儿就又恢复了原样。他没去医务室做检查，也不准备把这件事透露给任何人。近些年种种迹象都表明，预言正在一步一步地实现，信或不信的人心中都有自己的坚持，并不缺他手上这点信息。
他在梅洛彼得堡见过几个研究历史的犯人，数量不多，神志清醒时也常说些疯言疯语。他们说这是历史学家的通病，希望公爵大人不要介意。莱欧斯利当然不介意他们的措辞，他对他们的理论更感兴趣。按照某些说法，若世界总是盛极必衰，尔后再兴，那么那片吞没雷穆利亚的大海，也许总会归来的。这让预言听上去不再是预言，反倒像是依照某种规律得出的推论了。
他对是否相信这种理论持观望态度，就像对待很多其他事物一样。梅洛彼得堡中时常发生需要「调解」的事，同在现场的目击者很大概率会做出不一致的证词，所以莱欧斯利对所有存在的记录都保留意见。历史传记更是如此，为了所谓的史诗感夸大其词也是常态。「…就连海渊之下的巨龙也向他臣服…」…也许只是一条特大号龙蜥呢？
剔除这些光彩照人的部分，其余的才是他应当留意的地方。
在他尚未完结的人生中，莱欧斯利似乎总是在为某些目的做准备。无论何种情况下，他都不希望人们被恐慌支配。剔除了恐慌中的个人情绪后，留下的是一种叫危机意识的东西。为了应对危机，他总要做点什么，哪怕徒劳。
历史总是宏大的，这之下的人类与被海浪拍碎在沙滩上的贝壳毫无分别。他开始筹备制造维恩歌莱号，投入很多物资与人力，却并不对它抱有过高期待。这是一艘为了逃难而建的船，和带来文明与荣耀的金色法图纳号相距甚远。
但无论结果如何，假如能让这艘船成功开起来，那至少朱里厄和露尔薇的架没有白吵。
「…正如古代作家们曾说的那样，盛衰更替，无物恒常。」
EN: "But thusly do the ancient writers concur — 'Oceans will rise, empires will fall, and the only constant is change.'"

After dealing with the spies that the Fatui planted, Wriothesley took a bit of a swim in the seas around the Fortress. He spent very little time in there, finding afterward that his skin had flushed a slight red tint, though it returned to normal shortly afterward. He did not go to the infirmary for a checkup, nor did he intend to reveal this to anyone. All manner of recent signs had indicated that the prophecy was gradually coming to pass, and all people, regardless of whether they believed in it or not, had their own views on the matter, and did not really need this extra information.

He had encountered some inmates with academic research backgrounds, though their numbers were relatively few, and they were prone to mad babbling even when clear-headed. They called this a malady common to all historians, and begged his forbearance in the matter. Wriothesley, of course, did not mind, and indeed, he was very interested in their arguments. And according to some schools of thought, if rising and falling were common in this world, then that great sea that once swallowed Remuria may perhaps return someday. In that sense, the prophecy was not really a prophecy, then, but was instead the expression of a rational pattern.

As with many other things, he was somewhat on the fence about this reasoning. The Fortress was no stranger to issues that needed "mediation," with eyewitnesses often giving different testimonies. As such, he would reserve judgment on all records, and especially historical chronicles, for was poetic exaggeration not common practice in such writing? "Even the great dragon beneath the abyssal depths submitted to his power..." And how was anyone to know if this so-called great dragon was not just some very large vishap?
Once all embellishments were removed, what still remained were the actual things he needed to take note of.

Throughout his as-yet unfinished life, Wriothesley has always seemed to be preparing for something. No matter what, he does not wish for people to be ruled by terror. And once the personal element of fear has been removed, what remains is something more akin to a sense of danger. He would like to make some preparations in response to the crisis, even if it might prove futile in the end.

History is, after all, vast and terrible, and humanity is no more than seashells to be smashed upon the seashore by its great waves. Thus, he began to prepare for the creation of the Wingalet, expending vast resources and employing much manpower, though he did not put more stock into its success. It was a ship designed for fleeing disaster — an insurmountable chasm lay between it and golden Fortuna, bringer of civilization and glory.
Nonetheless, if it could indeed serve its purpose, Jurieu and Lourvine's many quarrels would not have been for naught.
"Thusly do the ancient writers concur — 'Oceans will rise, empires will fall, and the only constant is change.'"

CHS: 芙宁娜曾在枫丹的图书馆里读到一本冷门的书，故事的主角是一位在富丽堂皇的公馆中工作的侍从。
天真烂漫的少女谢贝蕾妲追寻报纸上的广告，来到深山野岭的公馆里应聘，虽有点笨手笨脚，但还是成为了这里的女仆。
公馆的主人不常出现，虽有喋喋不休的夫人与重视礼数的勋爵代为管理，少女在此的日子仍然很逍遥自在。
这里的人好像很久没有去过城里，于是女仆教他们唱最新的歌剧，玩最近流行的棋戏，侍从们的关系很快拉近，其乐融融。
唯有一条规则不容打破——通往地下室三层的沉重木门，封锁着只有公馆主人可知晓的秘密，无人允许接近。
女仆虽有好奇，但她更珍惜此地的精彩生活。时间悄然过去，某日从勋爵处得知主人即将来访，侍从们开始了繁忙的准备。
节日般的宴会热闹非凡，欢声笑语充斥于公馆各处，直到第二日女仆见主人迟迟未出现而前往查看，只见主人已经冰冷的尸骸。
警备队将嫌疑人锁定在众多侍从之中，焦急万分的女仆认为主人的死与公馆的秘密有关，最终决定打开那扇禁忌的大门。
没想到大门的对面竟然是公馆的正厅，站在中央楼梯前的是已然非常熟络的夫人，她发出的是一句熟悉又诡异的质问：
「你就是今天来应聘的，谢贝蕾妲吗？」
芙宁娜有些震撼，此处的情节似乎与记忆中类似的经历发生了共振。
她很羡慕女仆与侍从们愉快的日常生活，也敬佩她为了守护生活而直面秘密的勇气。
后来芙宁娜在梦中梦到了相同的公馆，她就是谢贝蕾妲，她气喘吁吁地跑到秘密的大门前，深吸一口气，还是将那门推开。
门后竟是汹涌灌入的海水，瞬间就将公馆淹没，无论是警备队，还是夫人和勋爵，也包括自己，都溶解得无影无踪。
芙宁娜由此惊醒，环顾四周之后，稍稍冷静，她不由得回忆这本书之后的故事——
谢贝蕾妲借由开门所引发的时间循环，破解了主人的死亡之谜，也掌握了公馆的秘密，为此地所有的住民都破除了古老的诅咒。
——她由衷感谢这位勇敢与坚韧的少女，给了故事一个好的结局。
而故事中几位塑造生动的人物形象，最终也从想象中诞生出可爱的模样，陪伴在芙宁娜的身旁。
EN: Furina once found a relatively unknown book in a library of Fontaine, and the story's main character was a servant working in an opulent mansion.

The idealistic young Mademoiselle Crabaletta, following a newspaper advertisement, came to a remote manor in the mountains to apply for employment, and despite her clumsiness, became a maid there all the same.
The Master of said mansion did not appear often, and though his loquacious surintendante and etiquette-minded gentilhomme managed it in his absence, she led a carefree life there.

None of the manor's attendants had been to the city in quite a long while, and so the maid taught them to sing the latest songs, play the latest tabletop games, and thus the servants grew closer and enjoyed one another's company.

There was but one ironclad rule, which was that none should approach the heavy wooden door that led three floors underground, behind which was locked a secret that only the Master of the mansion was privy to.

Though the maid was curious, she treasured her vibrant life there too much to pry. Time passed quietly, and one day, they were told by the gentilhomme that the Master was about to visit, and so the servants hurriedly began to prepare.

The banquet was akin to a festival, and laughter and cheer filled every corner of the mansion — at least, until the Master was late the second day, and upon investigating, the maid was to discover his already-cold corpse.
The Gardes narrowed the suspects down to the servants, but the maid, convinced that the Master's death had something to do with the mansion's secret, at last decided to open that forbidden gate.

To her surprise, what awaited her on the other side was the mansion's main hall, upon the central stairs of which stood the all-too-familiar surintendante of the house. The words she spoke, too, were bizarrely known to the maid.
"Ah, you must be our newest applicant. Crabaletta, I believe?"
Furina was quite dumbfounded when she read that, for the story here recalled similar events in her memories.
She admired the happy lives of the maid and the other servants, and the maid's courage in facing down the ancient secret to defend that life.
Later, Furina dreamt of that same mansion. In her dream, she was Crabaletta, huffing and puffing as she ran to that door of secrets, and, with one deep breath, pushed it open.
Behind it was a torrent of seawater that drowned the mansion in an instant, dissolving all in its wake — the Gardes, the surintendante of the house, the gentilhomme, and even herself.
Furina woke with a start, looking around her to gather her wits, and the rest of the story sprang to her mind, unbidden...
Crabaletta made use of the time loop triggered by opening the door to solve the mystery of the Master's death and discover the mansion's secret, freeing all its inhabitants from an ancient curse.
She thanked the brave, stalwart girl for giving that tale a happy ending.
And as for several vivid figures from the story, they would eventually be given lovely forms, that they might be by Furina's side.

CHS: 漫长的演出犹如轮回，谢幕之日遥不可及，只要预言危机尚存，这神明的故事就要延续下去。
即便长期以来枫丹人并没有对芙宁娜的身份产生怀疑，但她明白信任的崩塌始于小小的龟裂，一旦产生便不可逆。
被揭穿的代价是她无法接受的，长期以来的努力会变为徒劳，枫丹这个国度也将不复存在。
所以她努力在应该高兴的时候大笑，在应该悲伤的时候痛哭，在应该炫耀的时候夸张地彰显神明的身份，一刻都不敢放松。
芙宁娜知道这是一场演出，只要等她坚持到危机解除的时刻，她就可以脱去假面，拥有表达情绪的自由。
然而她逐渐意识到，她所扮演的属于神明应该有的样子，已经开始侵蚀她自身。
芙宁娜内心产生了一种令人恐惧的迷茫：如果在高兴的时候不去大笑，应该做出什么样的反应呢？
或许她原本不是很爱笑的女孩子，又或许她遇到一点挫折就会自暴自弃，但这些感情都已经逐渐消失了。
表演艺术家们总说，想要演好一个人物，就要先想办法成为那个人物。
从这个角度看，芙宁娜所扮演的水神是无可挑剔的，她的咬牙坚持收获了渴望的结果。
但从来没有人提到过表演结束之后的事，因为对他们来说，舞台仅仅是短暂的一瞬。
而芙宁娜演了太久，就连回去的路，都已经掩埋于风尘中，看不清了。
EN: Round and round the interminable performance went, the day of the curtain call ever beyond reach, but so long as the prophecy loomed, the tale of this god must go on.

Though Fontainians found no real reason to doubt Furina over the years, she knew that the collapse of trust could begin with a single crack. No matter how small, once it appeared, it would be irreversible.
And the consequences of being exposed would be to reduce all her long years of work to dust, to allow Fontaine to fall — that was unconscionable!

So she did her best to laugh loudly when she should be glad, and weep bitterly when she should grieve, and display the divine bearing of an Archon when it was time to show off, all without fail, all without rest.
She knew that this was a performance. If she could endure until the danger had passed, she could finally take off her mask and regain the freedom to express her feelings.
Yet, she slowly began to realize that the godly role she was playing was eating into her.
A horrifying doubt began to creep up on her — how should she react when glad, if not to laugh loudly?

Perhaps she was once a girl who did not much enjoy laughter. Perhaps she had once been the sort to give up on herself at the first sign of difficulty, but such emotions had already slipped away, bit by bit.
Those in the performance arts often say that one must become a character to play them.
From that perspective, Furina's performance as the Hydro Archon has been flawless. Her painstaking perseverance produced the perfect product.
But no one has ever spoken of what might transpire once the last light had dimmed, for to them, the stage is fleeting.
For one such as Furina, who has acted for far too long, even the path back offstage has faded into dust, buried by the sands of time.

CHS: 在时间凝滞的虚无之月中，万物仿佛都停止了流动。
时间并非真的停止，它只是缓慢到无法察觉，凡间的一日，似乎在这里要经过百年。
…一百五十一…一百五十七…一百六十七…
是的，是缓慢的时间，否则无法解释铭刻在脑中的回忆是被何物磨灭。
这些是什么意思？好像无论如何也不愿意忘记。
但这些是什么意思？但这些是什么意思？
那边的亮光是灯火吗？似乎见过很多次。
好像有谁反复说过，那就是家的方向。
总有一天能够回到家乡，这件事绝不能忘。
真孤单啊，这些数字，除了一，就只有自己。
就算忘记了名字，也不会忘记自己至少还存在。
EN: In the void moon, where time stands still, all things appear to have ceased their flow.
But time does not truly stop — it merely slows to the point of imperceptibility. A single day in the mortal world feels as though a century is passing here.
...One hundred and fifty-one... One hundred and fifty-seven... One hundred and sixty-seven...
Indeed, time must slowly pass — how else could one explain the erasure of the memories once engraved in my mind?
What do these things mean? It's as if I can't bear to forget them, no matter what.
But what do these things mean? What do these things mean?
Is that brightness over there the light from a lantern? It feels familiar.
It's as though someone once told me... It's the direction of home.
There will come a day when I can return to my homeland. This is something I must not forget.
So lonely... these numbers... Besides one, they have nothing but themselves.
Even if I forget my name, I won't forget that I exist.

CHS: 曾存在另一种可能性——用火种吸取阿佩普的力量，这样一来龙王死后对世界的影响也会减弱，从而保护须弥。
简直就像大反派会做的事。
（这样做虽然确实能解决眼下的危机，但在世界树遭到污染的时候，她就无法获得阿佩普的帮助了…）
（而且就像派蒙说的那样，我们都不可能做出这种选择。）
EN: There was a different possibility — using the Fire Seed to absorb Apep's power. The Dragon Sovereign's influence on the world would weaken after her death and Sumeru would be protected.
Only an evil villain would do that!
(I suppose that would have solved that particular crisis, but then when Irminsul became corrupted, she wouldn't have been able to call on Apep for help...)
(Besides, Paimon is right. None of us would have made a choice like that.)

title: 寄自彼岸的昨日·草和智慧：阿佩普方案的反事实代价

CHS: 嗯？你指的是什么…演出结束了么？我怎么好像想不起来发生了什么…
嗯…？不好意思，刚刚好像走神了，你是…
嗯，我想起来了，战友。看来我们猜得没错。
就像奥黛塔见到我死在军械宫的时候一样，被死之执政杀死后，因为某种原因大家最终还是会复活…
…只是会忘记死亡期间发生的事。
奥黛塔，还有大家应该都已经忘记了，为什么这次你能记得住？
难道…是因为这个？你说这是死之执政的符号吧？
我…好像什么也没看见啊。
欸…你看不见吗？这么说的话，死后世界的我刻在手上的东西，现实里确实应该看不到。
也就是说…这个符号被我刻在了灵魂里？让人感觉很不舒服啊，不过至少因祸得福，还能记得这些事情。
你呢，是因为你是死之执政口中的「降临者」么？
解释起来有些复杂，但确实就是这么回事。
现在终于算是告一段落了吧，可以整理一下现有的情报了。
首先能确定的是，这里的一切都还在我们「死前」的状态，证明死后世界的时间和现实时间并不对等。
我听说过人在死之前时间会放慢，短时间内回顾自己一生的说法。
说明那个时候已经半只脚踏入死后世界了吧？反正我们所经历的死后世界的那几天，应该只对应现实世界的短短几分钟。
这也符合之前关于军械宫人员大量短暂失忆的情报，如今看来，都是那位死神所说的「死之诅咒」导致的短时间死亡。
死而复生这件事，对不明真相的大家来说，感觉就像是丧失了某段时间的记忆。
那么现在的疑点是，所谓的「死之诅咒」究竟会在什么条件下触发？以及死亡之后又为什么会被复活？
至少证明杀死我们并非是她的最终目的，我们也还没搞清楚她「杀人」的理由。
嗯，这次由于剧院地脉的问题，她才需要特殊处理。从之前研究人员失忆的情况来看，杀死我们本来已经是家常便饭了。
说起来…我在「死」之前是不是正准备把什么东西记下来来着？
怎么也想不起来了…好像是和研究项目有关的东西…
不好意思，旅行者，我回头再联系你，我现在必须要回一趟军械宫了。
先生/女士，根据我曾经的一些调查，米提亚先生好像没有你这位朋友。
可是刚才你们二位好像聊得很熟络的样子…能告诉我他刚刚是匆忙准备去哪里吗？
哦顺便…我们两个是不是过去也有过些交集？恕我冒昧，只是隐隐觉得你身上似乎有种说不上来的「亲切感」。
我正准备说这件事。能麻烦你把剧院里的大家都召集起来吗？
大家再一次聚集在舞台上，只不过这次是在现实世界，剧院外的一切也没有被暴风雪吞没。
由于剧院地脉的特殊性，大家似乎没有将死后世界的经历彻底遗忘。
一切都像是遥远梦境中的回忆，不断被你的讲述所唤起，每个人都陷入了思考…
大家互相确认着自己的「命运」，直至今日的演出终于迎来散场。
EN: How are you holding up, Odette?
Hmm? What do you mean...? Is the performance over? I can't seem to recall what happened...
Hmm...? I'm sorry, I guess I spaced out there for a second. Remind me who you are...?
Yeah. I remember now, comrade. Looks like we guessed right.
Just like me when Odette found me at the Armory Palace... For some reason, everyone killed by the Ruler of Death eventually came back to life...
...Just with one catch: They forgot what happened while they were dead.
Odette and the others have already forgotten everything. Why were you able to remember this time?
Could... this be the reason? You said this is the Ruler of Death's symbol, right?
I... I don't see anything there.
You don't? Huh... Okay, I guess that makes sense. I carved this into my hand in the afterlife, so it's not visible in the physical world.
Does that mean I... carved this symbol into my soul? What an unsettling thought. Still, at least I get to remember what happened. I suppose it's a blessing in disguise.
What about you, though? The Ruler of Death mentioned that you're a "Descender," is that why you can remember?
A full explanation would get complicated very quickly, but that's essentially it.
Well, then. Now that it's all over, let's figure out what we've learned.
The first thing I notice is that everything here is precisely as we left it, right before our "deaths." This confirms that time passes differently in the afterlife than in the real world.
They say that right before death, time slows down and your whole life flashes before your eyes.
That must be how you know you have one foot in the afterlife by that point. Anyway, clearly the few days we spent in the afterlife probably only amounted to a few short minutes in the real world.

This also aligns with previous reports of widespread temporary memory loss among the Armory Palace personnel. Now, it seems likely that those were all brief deaths caused by the Grim Reaper's so-called "Curse of Death."
To those unaware of the truth, dying and coming back to life must feel similar to a short bout of catatonia.
This leaves me with a couple big questions. What are the conditions that trigger this so-called Curse of Death? And why are we resurrected after we die?
If nothing else, I think it shows that killing us wasn't her ultimate goal. We still don't know her true reasons for subjecting us to death.

Right. This time only got complicated because of the situation with the theater's Ley Lines — that's why she had to approach it differently. If the previous incidents of amnesia among the researchers are anything to go by, killing us is usually a pretty routine matter.
Come to think of it... Wasn't I about to note something down before I "died"?
I can't remember what it was, but... I think it was something related to my research project...
Sorry, 旅行者, I'll get back to you later. For now, I've got to make a trip back to the Armory Palace.
Sir/Ma'am, if I may... No one of your description has ever shown up in my investigations into Mr. Mitya's friends.
Yet you two seem very familiar with each other... Could you perhaps tell me where he was in such a rush to get to?
And by the way... have we ever crossed paths? Forgive the presumptuousness, but I feel a vague and indescribable sense of familiarity about you.
I can explain everything. Could you help me gather everyone in the theater in one place?
Everyone gathers onstage once again. But this time, you do so in the real world, without everything outside being devoured by a snowstorm.
Due to the unique properties of the theater's Ley Lines, it seems no one has completely forgotten their experiences in the afterlife.
As you recount the tale of what happened, people slowly begin to remember, as if accessing memories of a distant dream. Everyone is lost in thought...
Everyone confirms their own fate with each other, until finally today's show draws to a close.

title: 《槲寄生》·米提亚复核复活、时间与灵魂记号

CHS: 底部有着某种三分之一纹样的宝盒。如果能筹齐另外两个，或许可以打开何处的门。
「我已经很久没看过晴空与绿地了。不知道应该用什么样的蓝色、什么样的绿色，才能画出父亲想要的，冰雪消融的景象。」
「等他回来，一切都会恢复过去的样子吧。但是，太冷了。我已经不行了。」
「对不起，爸爸。对不起，一直看着我们丑态的乌库。」
「伊蒙洛卡，如果能再见你一面就好了…」
EN: A treasure box with a decorative pattern at the bottom. The ornamentation seems to be a part of a three-piece motif. Once the pattern is completed, a certain door may open.
"I'm afraid I can't finish the fresco."
"It's been a while since I last saw the blue sky and green grass. I don't know which hues to use to capture the landscape of thawing ice and snow that my father so longs for."
"By the time he comes back, everything will be back to how it was. But I can't take this cold anymore."
"Forgive me, Father. Ukko, I'm sorry you had to see us like this."
"Imunlaukr, I wish I could see you again..."

CHS: 呜哇！那些「雷灵」跟什么似的，我还以为是雷萤之类的魔物呢…
嗯…这些壁画好让人在意喔！上面的山，是鹤观这里的山吗？
那些星星标识的位置不知道有没有什么宝藏呢！
EN: Whoa, the way those Electro Seelie were chasing... whatever they were chasing around, you'd think they were Electro Cicins!
Huh. These murals are pretty interesting. Are the mountains painted here ones you can find on Tsurumi Island?
Paimon's wondering... Do those stars mark the positions of treasure or something?

CHS: 这里就是小呜斯之前说过的舞台吧？是我眼花了吗，这上面的壁画看起来还在动呢，好诡异！
该不会那些可怕的力量就是从这里跑出来的吧，小呜斯？
喂——小呜斯——噗嘶噗嘶？你在发呆吗？
难不成你以前也在这个舞台上演出过吗？所以觉得很怀念…之类的？
可能是也可能不是吧，都是过去的事了，也都是些无关紧要的事…
现在要紧的是，我能闻到空气中还残留着一丝不谐的气息，像是有某种令人感到不安的存在曾经到访此地。
但是更具体的…恐怕得先演奏这里的「曲谱」才能确定。
这里也有「曲谱」吗？我都没有注意到…
这样说来，你们虽然见过化形琴弦的「曲谱」，但还没见过壁画形式的「曲谱」呢，你面前的这个就是啦。
哦！原来因为是「曲谱」，上面的图案才会一动一动的吗？
是啦，我们之前不是找到过一本「空白曲谱」吗？接下来就是演奏了，先试试看吧。
EN: Is this the stage you spoke of earlier, Osse? And are Paimon's eyes deceiving her, or is the mural on top moving? It's kinda spooky...
That "terrifying power" couldn't be escaping from here, could it? Osse?
Hey! Osse! Ossssseeee! Are you spacing out?
...Ahem. My apologies. I was distracted for a moment.
Did you once perform on this stage? Is that why you're feeling, uh... nostalgic, or something like that?
I might have, or I might not. It was all in the past either way. Utterly irrelevant...
What matters now is the scent of discord I smell in the air. As though some presence, one that makes me uneasy, once visited this place.
I fear that specifics may only be ascertained once we have performed the "score" here.
There's one here too? Paimon didn't notice...
Well, you may have seen "scores" shaped like strings, but you have not seen those shaped like murals. One such is before you.
Oh! So the pictures are moving because it's actually a score?
Yes. Did we not find a "blank score" before? It is time now to perform it. Please, do the honors.
Perhaps you were an audience member.

title: 水下夜想曲·小呜斯、派蒙

CHS: 所以你们在下面发现什么了呢，快说给我听听！
你们将在下面的经历与发现告诉了玻娜…
欸？！你们是说在下面又找到了一枚火磷石？哇，我原本还以为我手上的是世上唯一的一枚呢。
等下，该不会我手上这枚其实是赝品吧…唔，难怪这么多年都没发现它有什么特殊的地方。
是啊，因为我们在下面找到的那块也一样，除了上面的花纹外没什么特别的。
哦对，我们还发现了一本奇怪的笔记，看起来像是以前来到这里的冒险家留下来的，你要看看吗？
冒险家的笔记？会来到这座诅咒之城的冒险家多半都是为了「回还之玉」而来，所以…我还是不看了吧。
嗯？但是上面提到了火磷石，还有祭坛的事情，说不定会是…
嗯嗯，我知道啦。就是因为这样，在找到「回还之玉」前，我才不想看那本笔记。
多年来有无数的冒险家为了寻找天蛇船和「回还之玉」而踏上征途…
但他们无一例外地都失败了，谁也没能证明那艘天空之船真的存在。
在人们看来，那或许只是个虚妄的梦，是饱受深渊之苦的人们所寄托的幻想。
所以他们的冒险不会被叙事人所记录，他们的事迹也不会被任何人歌颂。
如果无法找到天蛇船，无法拿到「回还之玉」的话，那他们所做的一切就都没有意义了！
是吗，你是这样认为的啊，你这种体验派的冒险家在纳塔可不多见哦。
虽说一事无成的冒险家也是存在的，但大部分人还是需要一些能够证明自己的东西的，不是吗？
你这种话是建立在真的存在那艘船的基础上的，假如世界上根本根本不存在什么天蛇船呢？
因此必须找到天蛇船才行，无论是为了老爹，还是为了其他曾为此付出生命的冒险家们。
而你们找到的那个笔记，无论究竟是谁留下来的，也只有在我们登上天蛇船之后，才会获得应有的价值。
所以哦，旅行者和小派蒙，要是我们真的能找到天蛇船然后平安回来，你们可要在那个冒险家协会好好宣传我们的事迹呀！
什么啦，你是想说我很擅长吹牛吗？要是我们真的找到了什么传说中的船，只要告诉凯瑟琳小姐都能传遍提瓦特了吧！
嗯嗯，毕竟我们也算是传奇冒险家呢，只要把我们的故事告诉哪个记者，马上就能上报纸的头条吧！
虽然它答应的是很开心啦，但它就算想要宣传也只能告诉龙冒险家吧…等等，龙里也会有冒险家吗？
哈哈，真好，不过说了这么多你们还没有把你们找到的那枚火磷石拿出来看看呢！
对哦，旅行者，快把火磷石拿出来吧，不知道绿宝看到之后能不能想起些什么来。
怎、怎么回事啊，眼睛都要晃瞎了！
哇，但是绿宝好像突然恢复了活力的样子！
看起来能使用「超能特攻光线」了。
嗯？旅行者，你是怎么能记住这么夸张的名字的啦。
不过确实，难道就像我们之前找到的那些能量碎屑一样，火磷石就是用来储存这种能量的…
看起来火磷石里也蕴藏着那种能量。
是哦，难道就像我们之前找到的那些能量碎屑一样，火磷石就是用来储存这种能量的…
然后也是因为有了这种能量，绿宝才能对付深渊的吗？
欸，又出什么事了？唔啊？！这个壁画怎么完全变样了！
看起来我们之前见到的壁画其实是覆盖在这个上面的呢。
在之前的壁画上也见到过…
是哦，这不就是我们在拿到第一块「通牒金盘」的遗迹里的壁画上也看见过的那条大黑龙吗？
看这上面画的，倒像是这条大黑龙才是这里的主人一样。
看这上面画的，倒像是那条坏龙才是这里的主人一样。
唔，绿宝想说什么，你对这幅壁画有什么印象吗？
欸，这次的光是指向天空…
嗯嗯，不会错了，源火祭坛一定就在那个方向，这座古城的最高处！
真的假的，每次你说得这么确定我就有点担心…
哎呀，就再相信我一次嘛，我有预感，这次一定不会错的！
竟然已经开始依靠预感了吗…不过好吧，现在也只能相信你了，我们上去看看吧。
EN: What did you find down there? Tell me all about it!
You tell Bona about everything that transpired below.
Huh!? You found another piece of Pyrophosphorite? Wow, and here I thought that the one I have was the only one in the world.
Wait, could mine be a counterfeit? ... Hmm, that might be why I haven't noticed anything special about it all these years.
The one we found down there looks ordinary too, other than the patterns on it.
Right, we found some strange notes left behind by an adventurer. Do you want to see 'em?
Adventurer's notes? The ones who came to this cursed city are likely here for the Jade of Return anyway, so... Yeah, no need, I think.
But there were mentions of Pyrophosphorite and the Altar. Maybe...
I know. That's exactly why I don't want to look at the notes before I find the Jade.
Over the years, many adventurers have set off to find the Tonatiuh and the Jade...
But they all failed, and no one has been able to prove the existence of the vessel in the sky.
Most think it's just a dream, an illusion. A fantasy that people suffering due to the Abyss find solace in.
So their adventures were never recorded by storytellers, and their deeds were never lauded.
If we cannot find the Tonatiuh and retrieve the Jade of Return, then everything they did would have been in vain.
You really think so? It's rare to find adventurers who emphasize the journey in Natlan.
Adventurers with no accomplishments do exist, but most adventurers need something to prove themselves, no?
Your point assumes that the ship actually exists. What if it's just a story?
That's why we must succeed. For my old man, and for the adventurers who lost their lives while trying.
As for the notes you found... Regardless of its origin, they won't have any significance until we board the Tonatiuh.
So, if we do find the vessel and return safely, make sure you two tell everyone at the Adventurers' Guild about what we've done, alright?
Don't worry, Paimon has a knack for such things.
What, are you trying to say that Paimon is good at exaggerating? Anyway, if we really do find the legendary ship, telling Katheryne will be as good as telling all of Teyvat!
Hehe, we are legendary adventurers, after all. Just give any journalist our story and we'll be all over the headlines!
Paimon's happy it agreed, but even if it wanted to say something, it can only talk to other Saurian adventurers, right? ...Wait, are Saurian adventurers even a thing?
Anyway... You haven't shown me the Pyrophosphorite that you found yet!
Right! 旅行者, show them the Pyrophosphorite! Maybe Coco will remember something when it sees the stone.
Wh—What's going on? The light! It stings!
Looks like firing the "Super Awesomesauce Laser" shouldn't be a problem.
Uh... How did you remember such a frivolous name?
But still, could this be the same phenomenon as the energy scraps we found before? As in, that energy can be stored in Pyrophosphorite?
Looks like Pyrophosphorites contain the energy as well.
Yeah, it's the same as what happened with those energy scraps from before...
And Coco, in turn, uses the energy stored within to fight the Abyss.
Whoa, what's happening!? The mural looks different now!
So this was covered up by the mural that we saw before...
We've seen this in another, previous mural...
Isn't that the big black dragon on the mural in the ruins where we got the first Golden Entreaty?
But in this painting, it looks like the black dragon is the master of this place.
The dragon entrenches itself above the city...
This painting sure does make it look like the evil dragon is the master of this place.
Coco? What is it? Do you know anything about this mural?
Huh. The light's pointing toward the sky this time...
Right, this is it. The Altar of Primal Flame must be in that direction, at the highest point of the ancient city!
Are you sure? Paimon gets worried whenever you sound so confident about something...
Just trust me once more, would ya? I have a good feeling about this!
Is that what we're relying on nowadays? Well, not that we have anything else to trust in, so... let's get up there.

CHS: （描绘着许多兰那罗一起，面对——抑或是背对——什么奇怪东西的情景。其中有一个金色的兰那罗…）
（不，壁画的内容似乎发生了改变。金色的兰那罗变成了两个。）
EN: (A mural of many Aranara with their fronts — or backs — facing something strange. There's a golden Aranara with them...)
(No, there seems to be a change in the mural. There are two golden Aranara now.)

title: 森林书·往昔的桓那兰那壁画调查

CHS: …人类乃是立于「进化」之顶点的生命，人类乃是地上一切生灵演化的终点…
…大火山的龙蜥曾自视为掌握了进化的种族，然而他们已在漫长无序的演化中丢失了智慧，继而又失去了力量，最终沦为任人宰割的野兽…
…火龙蜥的退行进化证明，龙的族裔已经被「进化」之道所抛弃。它们的子嗣失去了源火的纯粹，火的君主也不再会从它们当中诞生了…
…在他的带领下，人类统治了大地。而终有一天，我们还会征服天空，因此决不可被夜之国束缚…
…有幸登上这艘天船的人们啊，踏出我们伟大事业的第一步吧…
【石碑上浮现出了原本不可见的燃素字迹。】
（若不是因那独断的天罚，分化我的族类，断绝了他们进化的道路，我又为何要在人类身上寻找「进化」的可能。受造的人们啊，你们是永远无法理解的，因为你们只是「进化」中的一环。）
EN: ...Humanity is the apex life form, the final destination of all things that live in this world...

...The vishaps of the Great Volcano once held themselves masters of evolution, but they lost their wisdom in their lengthy, chaotic adaptations, and with it, their power, becoming but beasts to be slaughtered by humans...

...The devolution of the Pyro Vishaps proves that dragon-kind has been abandoned by the evolutionary path. Their heirs have lost the primal flame's purity, and the sovereign of fire shall never again be born from amongst them...
...Under his guidance, humanity came to rule the land, and one day, we shall conquer the heavens also. Thus, be not bound by the realm of Night...
...Those upon whom have been bestowed the fortune of boarding this ship, go ye forth! Take the first step toward the realization of our great cause...
[Phlogiston inscriptions that could not be seen previously emerge.]

(Were it not for the arbitrary divine punishment that divided my race and cut off their evolutionary paths, why would I have needed to seek new possibilities in humanity? Oh humanity, you who were created, you will never understand, for you are but one stage in this "evolution.")
JP: …同胞たちよ、肝に銘じよ…
…人類は「進化」の頂点に立つ生命にして、地上にいるあらゆる生物の進化の終点。
…かつて、大火山のヴィシャップは、己を進化を掌握した種族だと自負したが、長く無秩序な進化の過程で知性を失い、力を失い、ついには人に殺されるだけの野獣となった…
…炎のヴィシャップの退行と進化は、龍の末裔がすでに「進化」の道に見放されたことを示している。源火の純粋性を失った彼らの子孫から、炎の君主が生まれることもなくなった…
…彼の導きのもと、人類は大地を統治した。そしていつか、我々は天空をも征服する。だから、夜の国に縛られてはならないのだ…
…この空飛ぶ船に乗ることができた幸運な人々よ、我々の偉大なる事業の第一歩を踏み出そう…
【石碑には、これまで見えなかった燃素の文字が浮かび上がった。】
（あの独断の天罰によって我が種族が分化せず、彼らの進化の道を断たれていれば、我が人類の中に「進化」の可能性を求めることも無かっただろう。創造されし人類たちよ、汝らは永遠に理解できないだろう。なぜなら、汝らは「進化」の一部に過ぎないのだから。）
KR: …동포들이여, 명심할지어다….
…인간은 「진화」의 정점에 있는 생명체이며, 또한 지상에 존재하는 모든 생명체 진화의 종점이다….
…한때 대화산의 용 도마뱀은 스스로를 진화를 정복한 종족이라 자칭했으나, 길고도 무질서한 진화의 과정에서 지혜와 힘을 잃은 끝에 인간에게 도살당하는 짐승으로 전락하고 말았다….
…불 용 도마뱀의 퇴행성 진화는 용의 후예가 「진화」의 길에서 탈락했다는 사실을 증명한다. 그들의 자손은 근원의 불의 순수성을 상실했으며, 불의 군주 또한 더 이상 그들 사이에서 태어나지 않는다….
…그의 인도 아래 인간은 대지를 통치했다. 그리고 언젠가 우리는 하늘마저 정복할 것이니, 절대 밤의 나라에 속박당해서는 안 된다….
…이 하늘선에 탑승한 행운아들이여, 이제 우리의 위업을 시작하자….
[비석에 지금까지는 보이지 않았던 열소 글자가 나타났다]
(그 독단적인 천벌 때문에 내 종족이 분열되고 진화의 길이 끊기지 않았다면… 내가 무엇하러 인간에게서 「진화」의 가능성을 찾았겠는가. 창조된 인간들이여, 「진화」의 일부에 지나지 않는 너희는 영원히 이해할 수 없을 것이다)

CHS: 底部有着某种三分之一纹样的宝盒。如果能筹齐另外两个，或许可以打开何处的门。
「老身本以为后代能如白树一般生生不灭。」
「但白树即将枯死，『他们』的声音不再传来，老身的期待、他们于此身的期待也即将落空。」
「老身将再次登上峰顶，寻求指引。下山时，女儿第二幅画应该已经完成了。」
「第三幅画，若是冰雪消融的图景就好了。」
EN: A treasure box with a decorative pattern at the bottom. The ornamentation seems to be a part of a three-piece motif. Once the pattern is completed, a certain door may open.
"I thought that the young will grow strong and vital like cypresses."
"But these cypresses are about to wither. Their voices won't be carried by the wind anymore. My expectations towards them, as well as the faith they have in me, will all fall through."
"Once again I'll climb this peak looking for guidance. By the time I'm back down, my daughter will have finished the second painting."
"As long as the third one will be of thawing snow and ice, everything will be fine."

CHS: 「…已殁。再没有书记的必要了。最大的憾事，莫过于无法目睹她完成大殿中的壁画吧…」
EN: "...ended. There is no more need for records. Yet I regret nothing more than having been unable to watch her finish the fresco within that great hall..."

title: 龙脊雪山石碑·记录者的遗憾

CHS: 又见面了，旅行者！还有…那个…
顺便一问，这个飞来飞去的小家伙怎么卖？看上去蛮有趣的。
明显不太好吧！这家伙怎么突然失忆了！
哈哈哈哈…咳咳…哈哈哈哈哈！瞧瞧…瞧瞧你们那副表情！噗哈哈哈哈哈！
完了…我笑岔气了…对不…对不起…这是…呵哈哈哈哈…这是我最喜欢的「健忘笑话」！
噗…好了，好了，不开玩笑了，抱歉抱歉。
真是的，我还以为你作为大冒险家，是个很严肃的人呢！
呵呵，可不要产生这样的刻板印象哦，冒险家协会可是有名的怪人圈子。我在里面算是比较正常的呢。
还是谢谢你们的蘑菇。这东西到现在为止效果还不太明显…或许是需要长期服用，也许本身就不是什么药物…总之味道不差就是了。
这些可不能全吃完了，我还要留一些给须弥的朋友，帮忙研究一下它的药用价值。
我猜你一转头就会把这事忘了…
咳咳，正事正事。请问二位有没有去寻找壁画呢？
哦哦，大恩不言谢！这个国家是这样表达感谢的，对吧？
唔嗯…有趣，非常有趣。只是…你们没有发现更多壁画了吗？
鹤观的原住民曾以雷元素之魔鸟为信仰，以祭祀仪礼为核心组建起自己的文明。稍微了解历史的人对此应该并无异见…
但在你们提供的壁画上…却没有雷鸟的痕迹。人们所膜拜的是另一些东西——
日月星辰…和…奇怪的符号。或许…在雷鸟降临之前，鹤观原住民的先祖们就已经拥有了一定高度的文明…
除此之外…雾与月亮，群星与黑暗…唔，解释不通呢…
还是不要过度用脑了吧…你的记性已经很不行了。
…啊，抱歉。思考太入迷，忘了你们还在场。
再次感谢你们的辛劳，我接下来的日志有了足够的素材…假如能有幸被历史学者重视的话，我是不会忘记署上二位的大名的！
好了，我也该去冒险家协会报道了。实在抱歉打扰了你很长时间，希望下次有缘再见。
啊，顺便…还有一件事。虽然不是什么大事，但希望你能替我关注一下。先前提到的那个小孩子…叫…什么来着…
「阿瑠」…对，是这个名字。我这次顺便给那孩子带了些吃的…希望还新鲜。
自从上次以来，我还一直惦记着这岛上有个孩子…在这样凶险的岛上过日子，一定很不容易吧。
好了，不多耽误你时间了，旅行者。旅途的下一站再见，向着星辰与深渊！
这是「健忘人」适应这个世界的方式。
对呀，对呀！怎么还恶化了！
EN: We meet again, 旅行者, and your, uh, um...
Could I ask what you'd sell this flying fellow for? I think she's quite interesting!
He's clearly not alright! This guy's having that amnesia thing again!
What on earth are you saying... *hurk*
Hahahaha! *cough* Ahahah! Just... Just look at the looks on your faces! Hehahah!
I'm done... I'm out of breath... S—Sorry... This... Ahahaha... This is a favored "joke" of mine, you know?
I'm afraid I don't get your sense of humor.
*cough* Alright, alright, no more jokes. I'm sorry.
Really! Paimon thought a famous adventurer like you would be a more serious person!
Haha. It might be best not to have too fixed a view of adventurers. The Guild is well-known as a circle of oddities. I'd even call myself "normal" amidst their ranks.

Still, thank you for those mushrooms. Their effects haven't been all that evident so far. Perhaps they need long-term use to really take effect, or maybe they don't have medicinal properties at all... But either way, they taste pretty good.
I should be careful not to finish all of these. I need to leave some for my friend in Sumeru who can help to research any medicinal properties that they may have.
I feel like you're just going to forget this...
*cough* Ahem, well, back on topic. Have the two of you gone looking for the murals yet?
Well, here's the photos that you wanted.
Ooh, my thanks for your most generous aid!
Let's see. Interesting, very interesting. Hmm... Did you find any other murals?
Hmm, that's even more interesting, then.

The people of Tsurumi Island used to worship a monstrous bird that wielded the power of Electro, and their civilization was centered around rituals and other ceremonial affairs to this effect. Most people who know something of history do not contest this view...
But the murals that you've provided show no sign of the Thunderbird's presence at all. It seems that the people worshiped something else altogether—

That is to say, the sun, moon, and stars... and whatever these strange symbols represent. Perhaps Tsurumi Island's natives already had a certain degree of civilization before the Thunderbird's descent...
Other than those, the fog and the moonlight, the stars and the darkness... Hmm, I can't explain these...
Best not to use your head too much, Roald. Who knows what that'll do to your memory...
...Ah, yes. Sorry. I was lost in thought. Barely even noticed you two, really.

Thanks once again for your hard work. I think this much is enough for me to write my next diary... If it gets picked up by some historians, I won't forget to add the two of you to the acknowledgments section!
Alright then. I think it's time I reported back to the Guild. Sorry for all the time I've taken up. May we meet again!
Ah, right. There is one other thing. Nothing major, mind, but I hope that you could help me look out for someone. It's that child I mentioned earlier, whose name was... Um... Give me a moment...
Right, "Ruu." That was his name. I brought some things along this time for him to eat... I hope they're still fresh.
Ever since the last time I came here, I've been thinking about that kid. I can't imagine that life has been easy for him on such a perilous island.
Alright, you'll hear no more from me. Let us meet again on the next leg of our respective journeys, 旅行者! Ad astra abyssosque!
These were all we could find.
I guess this is how forgetful people survive, eh?
Did the Fluorescent Fungus from before work?
That's right! Why does it seem like he's gotten worse instead!?

title: 健忘大王历险记·罗尔德

CHS: …很奇怪吧！而且，上面画的祭司人像，也不像又爷爷他们。
姑且听听他们在说什么吧…
哦哦，是木户哥的猜想时间！这回又有什么大胆的想法呢？
那些壁画是在有雾海之前的时代画的。在好久好久以前，世界上没有雾，所以大家看得到上面有什么东西！
在上面，有那些圆形的、星形的东西，还有那个像山一样的东西！所以古代的壁画上，会画这些！
木户哥的想象力真丰富！
不过，千万不要让又爷爷…还有宇奈婆婆听到！不然，又要被说啦。
圆形的、星形的…他们说的壁画上的形状，会是月亮和星星吗？这里的雾气这么大，确实看不到呢。
原来鹤观的小孩子是这么想的呀…不知道他们还有什么想法呢？
EN: ...That's just weird. And the priests on the drawings up there don't look like Grandpa Mata or the others at all.
They're not paying us any mind at all! Paimon's gonna get mad!
We might as well listen in...
Hah, it's time for Big Brother Kito's wild guesses! Alright, what've you got this time?
These murals depict a time before the Sea of Fog. A long, long time ago, there was no fog over the world, so everyone could see what was up there!
Up there, they could see these round- and pointy-shaped things, and these mountain-like things! That's why these ancient murals look the way they do!
That's some imagination you've got there, Kito!
But not a word of this to Grandpa Mata or Granny Una! We'll be in for an earful otherwise...
"Round- and pointy-shaped things"... Are they talking about the moon and stars depicted here on the mural? The fog's so thick here, it's no wonder that they couldn't see 'em.
So the children of Tsurumi Island thought this way, huh. Paimon wonders what else they believed?

title: 倾听木簧笛的八音曲·木户

CHS: 拓绘壁画而成的画卷，绘有雾海之中的山岳，深远的画面中似乎隐藏着某种难以明辨的信息。
传说鹤观的古代原住民会用颜料将无法追忆的古老历史涂画在山洞内的岩壁上，存续千年而完好如初。透过这些壁画，方可了解鲜为人知的往事…
EN: A replica made of a certain mural that depicts a mountain within an ocean of fog. This picture seems to hide some indecipherable meaning.

It is said the ancient natives of Tsurumi Island would use paints to depict ancient, now-unremembered history onto the rock walls of caves, and that these murals have remained pristine to this day. One might be able to learn more about an unknown past through this mural...

title: 壁画拓印-「雾海孤岳」·摆设说明

CHS: 旅行者哥哥/姐姐真厉害，一下就让青苔缩回去了，就像对付氲气的时候一样！
不过，明明上次来的时候还没有的呀，这也是自然吗…
没关系！不管是青苔还是丘丘人，交给旅行者都没问题的！小茂，这幅画里说的是什么呢？
哼哼！一开始，我也不懂画的是什么，但今天听了浮锦姐姐说的故事，我就想到了。这里的是灵濛山的壁画之前的事情！
你看，很久很久以前，那时候的人还能和天上的神仙沟通，应该就是对着中间那个很大的玉。
当中，还有神明的使者带领他们、保护他们。派蒙姐姐你看，应该就是这里画的这名金人，闪闪发光的，又站在最前面，一定是最厉害的人。
后来，就像浮锦姐姐说的，发生了异变，沉玉谷的祖先失去了导引的使者，也不再能和天上的神仙对话。后来，才有了投珑的仪式。
嗯？小茂说的很有道理呢！
嘿嘿，谢谢派蒙姐姐。旅行者哥哥/姐姐觉得呢？
这么一想，就觉得祖先好厉害。那时候留下来的玉，到今天都还有力量，能够恢复自然呢！这么古老的东西都这么厉害，以前一定比现在要好吧！
不是的。世界一直在进步。
…而过去的积累是无价的宝物。
哦…旅行者哥哥/姐姐真的好厉害，我从来没有像你那样考虑过问题。
唔，我觉得小茂才厉害。我们在冒险中见到了好多好多古代的东西、古代的谜题、古代的神秘力量、古代的怪物，我从来没想过这些…
嘿嘿。派蒙姐姐不考虑这些事情，也好厉害，真的！派蒙姐姐长大了一定也跟我的姐姐一样，是个开开心心到处去冒险的人！
倒也不是亲姐姐啦！她在沉玉谷工作过一段时间，天天往山上、河边跑，我也跟着她到处跑，这个小洞也是和她一起发现的呢！
她说，这个小洞就是我的「卢鼻孔河」！虽然我也不知道这个「卢鼻孔河」是什么意思啦…
…但即使如此也不能放弃未来。
EN: You're awesome, 旅行者! You pushed the moss back just like that — like you did with that smoky cloud!
Still, that wasn't there yesterday. Is this what they call "nature"...
Don't worry about it. Moss or hilichurls, just leave 'em all to 旅行者! Little Mao, what's this picture about?
Hehehe! Originally, I didn't know either, but I figured it out today after hearing Big Sis Fujin's story! This must be the stuff that happened before the mural on Mt. Lingmeng was made!
See this? Long, long ago, people were able to talk to the gods and adepti in the skies by talking to that big piece of jade in the middle.
The emissary of the gods would lead them and protect them. See, that's gotta be this shiny golden person standing in the middle — I bet that was a super amazing person.

But later, just like Big Sis Fujin said, something changed, and the people of Chenyu Vale lost their guiding emissary, and they couldn't talk to the heavens any longer — that's how the Rainjade Rite came about.
Huh. Your story does make sense!
Hehe, thanks! What do you think, 旅行者?
You're a pretty bright spark, Little Mao.

Come to think of it, our ancestors were pretty amazing themselves, huh? The jades they left to us still have the power to restore nature! For something this old to still be so strong, the past must've been a sweller time than the present, huh?
That's not true. The world marches onward.
...Leaving the accumulated detritus of the past in its wake.
Huh... That's a really cool thought. I never thought about it that way.

Hehe, Paimon thinks that you're the amazing one, Little Mao. We've seen lots of ancient objects, puzzles, mysterious powers, and monsters in our time, but Paimon's never considered this stuff before...
Hehe. Oh, you know what? Not thinking about this stuff at all is pretty awesome too, really! I bet you'll be just like my big sister when you grow up, just having fun adventuring everywhere!
Ooh, you have a big sister, then?
Well, we're not blood-related, but she worked here in Chenyu Vale for a while. She'd go up mountains and run around the rivers, and I'd follow her! We discovered this little cave together!
She said that this cave is my "Rubicon"... Not that I know what that means...
That's right. The world's been constantly in decline.
...But even so, we shouldn't give up on the future.

title: 祀珑在昔，灵锦歆诚·小茂

CHS: 这里曾经很是热闹，香火也十分旺盛…那时我们三个尚且能够在山野河川自在穿行。
是啊…那是如同月下流水一般，虽然灰暗，但也闪闪发光的时日…
多亏了你们，我才能再一次回到这里，主持投珑的仪式。
咦？这么说…浮锦仙人是那个壁画里的人物？
喔，我知道了，浮锦姐姐就是那个那个，站在山顶，抱了个蛋的？
啊——真是的，小茂！那可是宝玉，怎么就是蛋了！
「投珑」是充满了力量的仪式。祀珑可以让河川平静、风调雨顺，但也可以成为杀伐之物。就像一路上帮助你们的仙力，与它一纸之隔的就是咒力。
我要牢牢把握着投珑仪式，以免有人以它为恶。所以，咳咳…没错，小仙我就是壁画里那个「抱了个蛋的」。
是喔…那这样的话，浮锦姐姐确实很古老呢。
嗯。不过，我还是比较喜欢小茂管我叫「姐姐」，听起来比较年轻呢！
呵呵，那当然！只是被人们称为「仙人」…我自知和理水叠山他们那些真正的仙人比起来，可差得太多啦。
和我的朋友们比起来，我也是最弱小的一个。我既不能制药救死，也不能骋足山野。但是，即使如此，也不能因为明白这个，就放下仙人的架子。
不然呀，那样才对不起沉玉谷的人们。
不过，你们爱怎么叫我就怎么叫我，不必介怀。毕竟，我们…应该说，我觉得，我们已经是朋友了。
何况，被奉为仙人的日子，都已经是过往啦，就和这个地方一样。
在过去，投珑仪式是欢庆的节日，这里可热闹了。我们庆祝丰年，用笑声、炮仗和兽舞吓跑灾年。如今在人们看来，这里只是被遗忘的古遗迹。
嗯，之前在翘英庄里，就有人跟我们说了浮锦仙人打败妖怪，种下茶树的故事，竹筏上也提过陆爷爷说奉茶典仪是给某个鲤鱼仙人奉献的仪式呢。
在遗珑埠不是还有人唱戏，讲的大鲤鱼杀来杀去的故事吗？故事里的浮锦姐姐，那可厉害了！而且，现在还有人会舞兽呀！
况且你也说过，「仙人」的定义…
而且，先不论定义，浮锦仙人确实是我们的朋友呀！所以，你要开开心心的！也别老想着投珑仪式什么的，就当做是朋友一起冒险吧！
嗯…嗯！说得真好。谢谢你们！再说了，明明是我拜托你们帮忙的，我自己不打起精神，一个劲在这里怀旧，那怎么行呢！
那么，为了准备仪式，还需要麻烦你们帮忙。
先前你们四处冒险时，不知是否遇到过「仙像」呢？那是古时常用的仪式精灵，当时的人们常常用它守护家宅。这周边应当也有仙像。
旅行者、派蒙，还有小茂，拜托你们将周边的仙像安置好。如此，就能为投珑仪式协调好此地的灵脉了。
EN: Much time has passed since I last emerged here.
This was once a lively place, filled with the aroma of incense... Then, the three of us could travel freely across the mountains and rivers.
Yes... Those days were like flowing water 'neath the moon, dark, yet sparkling oh so brightly...
Thanks to you all, I am now able to return here and host the Rainjade Rite.
Eh? So... you're that person in the mural?
Oh, I get it now! That person... standing on the mountain, hugging that egg, that was you, wasn't it?
Ah— An egg? Come now, Little Mao, that was precious jade!

"Casting Rainjade" is a ritual of great power. The Votive Rainjade can calm rivers, improve the weather... But it can also be a thing of death and slaughter. Only the thinnest line separates curses and the adeptal energies that have aided you up till now.

That is why I must make sure that the Rite does not fall into the hands of those who would do ill. That's why... Ahem, yes, that is correct, one was indeed the figure who "hugged that egg" in that mural.
Huh... Big Sis Fujin, doesn't this make you pretty, uh, ancient?
Yes, it does. Still, I do like the name "Big Sis." It does quite make me feel young!
Well, being called "adeptus" is pretty alright too.
Well, certainly! Though even if others title me as such, I am aware that I am hardly the equal of true adepti like Mountain Shaper and the rest.
I am, in truth, the weakest of my band of friends. I cannot make medicines to save others, nor can I bound across the mountains and plains. Even so, I could not simply lay the title down.
It would have done the people of Chenyu Vale a disservice, I fear.
Still, you may call me whatever you wish. After all, we... have become friends, or so I would say.
In any case, my days of being called an adeptus are now consigned to history, just like this place has been.

Once, the Rainjade Rite was a day of great celebration, where we would commemorate the year of abundance, using laughter, firecracker battles, and beast dances to frighten the ill omens away. This must appear like naught but forgotten ruins to the modern mind.

That's right. People in Qiaoying Village told us that it was the mighty Adeptus Fujin who defeated the demons and planted the first tea tree. Back on the bamboo raft, Grandpa Lu also mentioned that the offerings of tea were to a certain Carp adeptus.

And wasn't there that opera sung at Yilong Wharf about the Carp going around killing stuff? Hehe, you were so awesome in those stories, Big Sis Fujin! Also, people still do the Wushou dance, you know!
You said it yourself. The definition of an "adeptus" is...
Also, putting definitions aside, you're our friend, Fujin! You shouldn't be constantly fretting about the rite and stuff. You should live happily — like we're companions on an adventure!
That's right, we're on an adventure together!
Right... Yes, you're right! Thank you — that was well said! Indeed. I was the one who asked you all for help. It wouldn't do at all if I just continued wallowing in the past, now would it?
In any case, I'll need your help to prepare for the Rite itself.
In any case, have you encountered any Sacred Simulacra in your adventures? Those were ritual spirits often used by people in ancient times to protect their homes. There should be some nearby.
旅行者, Paimon, Little Mao, please help me put the Simulacra in their proper places. That way, we can restore the spirit veins using the Rainjade Rite.
I will. I have faith in you.
Well, being called "adeptus" is pretty alright too... right?

title: 祀珑在昔，灵锦歆诚·浮锦

CHS: 我？我当然没事，不仅如此，我可是好得很呐，从出生到现在，没有哪一刻像现在这样好过！
派蒙和旅行者来自异乡，不了解它的价值，可以理解。
哲伯莱勒和婕德，唔…疏于学问？不，这原本也不是他们应该知道的东西。
派蒙，我来考考你，你从这幅壁画上得到了什么信息？
唔…画上有很多人？还有…还有又像是太阳又像是眼睛的东西…
唉，看来派蒙确实没什么做学问的天分。
既然知道就不要问我嘛！
那旅行者呢？你在这幅壁画上看到了什么？
是很对称…但这不仅仅是一种艺术风格，也象征了一种稳固的结构，并且是一种稳固的「权力结构」。
太阳，还有眼睛，象征着赤王本身。在他之下，也就是所谓的「七柱」，为赤王撑起了权力之塔。
而他的子民…那些渺小的人，不敢有丝毫怨言，只能顺从地对其表示臣服。
虽然即便如此，他们也未能逃脱毁灭的命运…
我说的还能有错？这幅壁画所表达的主旨，完全符合我看过的那些文献中所写的赤王形象。
一个用绝对的、至上的权力，将所有子民都纳于视线之下，令人战栗的恐怖君王。
欸？可是我觉得，这幅壁画，给人一种很平和的感觉呢。感觉一切都井然有序，大家都各司其职，不也挺好的吗？
什么？这是什么歪门邪道的解读。
…婕德，你要胡乱编些奔奔跟门聊天之类的瞎话是没问题，但是要说到对壁画，对赤王文明历史的解读，那可是我的领域。
没什么可是，我所说的内容，都是有先行研究佐证的，而这里的壁画本身，之后也将成为我们因论派研究的一部分。
这部分，当然，就由我来书写。
婕德并不全对，但是你，对沙子知道得太少。
哈！一路上都没见你说过几次话，现在跳出来为女儿抗辩吗？虽然要论武力，我当然是比不过你，可我还有旅行者！
旅行者，你会站在我这边的，对吗？
这不合适吧！大家都是一起旅行…不，一起考古的伙伴，就算意见不一样，也不至于要大打出手吧？
啊？什么一起？这次考古可是由我发起，由我出资，你们全都受我雇佣。
而且，只有我是经过正统学术训练的，说起学术问题，怎么轮得到外行置喙？
…只是拾人牙慧可称不上是独当一面的学者。
哦？这么说，那我倒要听听你有什么「独到的」见解。
这个已经覆灭的国度，曾经也是牢固美丽的，让人不敢相信…这一切竟然建立在漫沙之上。
而你，你只看到了表面的顺从，却忽视了愿望的朝向。
黄沙的子民靠着愿望与赤王紧密相连，原以为这样便可以抵御一切灾祸。只是结果，我们现在都知道了。
妄想也要有个限度，你这是想推翻前人的全部研究成果吗？我可不认为目前有足够的证据支持你的妄想。
巧了，我也不认为自暴自弃孤注一掷来到此地的落魄学者称得上是学术权威。
真看不出你原来是如此牙尖嘴利之人…
再吵下去也不会有结果的。
对啊…虽然搞不懂你们在吵什么，但是学术上的问题，肯定都有讨论的余地，对吧？现在就先把意见不一样的地方放一放…
反正谁也说服不了对方。
嗯，那我们就继续深入调查一下嘛！说不定…呃，说不定之后还有更多线索呢，到时再来看看谁对谁错也不迟吧？
哎！气死我了，真不该跟外行讨论学术问题！
看起来像是向上的通道。
不知道会通向什么地方呢…不过，待在原地也是不会有什么结果的，我们继续前进吧，好吗？
渺小的臣民和伟大的王。
没错！这幅壁画正象征着这样一种「权力结构」！
EN: Me? Of course I am. I'm terrific! I've never felt better!
Since Paimon and 旅行者 aren't from around here, it's understandable that you don't recognize its worth.
As for Jebrael and Jeht, uh... I guess it's a knowledge issue? No, it isn't something you should have knowledge about.
Paimon, let me test you for a moment. What can you discern from this mural?
Uh, there are many people? And... and something like a sun and an eye...?
*sigh* I guess Paimon has no talent for this.
Why did you even ask if you already knew that, huh!?
And what about you, 旅行者? What do you see in this mural?
Hmm... It's a very symmetrical painting?
It is symmetrical... But this isn't a matter of style alone. It symbolizes a solid structure, a rule by force.
The sun and the eye symbolize King Deshret. Beneath him are the "seven pillars," so we call them, that hold up King Deshret's pyramid of authority.
As for his subjects... They are insignificant. They dare not express any complaint. They are forced to submit.
But even so, they couldn't escape destruction...
Hmm... Is that really the case?
Come now, how can I be wrong? The theme of this mural fully conforms to the depictions of King Deshret in everything I've ever read.
A terrifying king who used absolute and supreme authority to keep all his subjects beneath him.
Hmm... But this mural feels so peaceful to me. Everything feels so orderly, and everyone has their own place and duty. Isn't that good?
What? What kind of crooked interpretation is that?
...Jeht, you can make up stories about Benben talking to doors, but deciphering murals and the history of King Deshret's civilization is my area of expertise.
Now, I won't hear any buts. Everything I have said has been proven by prior research... and this mural will become part of Vahumana too.
Of course, I'll be the one to write it.
Jeht isn't entirely correct, but you... You know very little about the sand.
Ha! You've hardly said more than a few words all this time, yet you're standing up for your daughter now? I may not be a match for you in a battle of strength, but I have 旅行者 by my side!
旅行者, you'll take my side, won't you?
That's not appropriate! We're all traveling together... No, we're all companions on this expedition. Even if our opinions differ, we shouldn't fight over it, right?
What? Together? I started this expedition, and I paid for it. All of you are employed by me.
Moreover, I'm the only one with formal academic training. A layman has no right to speak on academic issues!
...One who only draws from others can hardly call himself an independent researcher.
